"The Addis Ababa Museum stands as a beacon of Ethiopia's rich cultural heritage, offering an immersive experience for those eager to explore the nation's history. Located in the bustling capital, this museum is a must-visit for tourists seeking to deepen their understanding of Ethiopian culture. The museum's extensive collection includes artifacts, art pieces, and historical documents that narrate the diverse narratives of Ethiopia's past, from ancient civilizations to contemporary society. Visitors will find themselves captivated by the intricate displays that highlight Ethiopia's unique contributions to art, science, and social development."

I highly recommend it to anyone interested in art, history, or culture.

user_reviews.Name: Amer Salih
user_reviews.Description:
Addis Ababa museum in Meskel Square is a quiet, small museum located just behind the Red Terror Martyrs Memorial museum. This museum has two entrances, one through the Meskel Square area where you have to pay 20 Ethiopian birr to enter the square itself and then 20 more birr to enter the museum (1 united states dollars ~ 100 Ethiopian birr). The other entrance is near the Red Terror Martyrs Memorial museum where you do not have to pay the 20 Ethiopian birr fee to enter the Meskel Square area (but I highly recommend entering this area because it has lots and lots of activities and food cars).

The museum itself is small with rooms where they display actual royal clothes and artifacts with explanations to everything you see. You'll also get to know much of the history of the city of Addis Ababa (lit; the new flower).

After the rooms of the clothes you get to see photos and weapons (guns, sords and shields) used by the Ethiopian army to defend the city against the Italian colonial army. Also you get to contemplate various coin collections and beautiful artifacts.

After completing the inner rooms of the museum, never forget to check out the art gallery upstairs where they host beautiful paintings and sculptures, some of them for sale. There's also another room just above the museum's rooms where they display many paintings given to the museum.

The place has a nice green area in front of the entrance and a very fancy restaurant outside.
I'd pay the 20 birr for this area by itself cause it's very green and looks right above Meskel Square.

I'd also pay the 20 birr to experience the Meskel Square area and the various entertaining activities there, especially the rental bicycles.

user_reviews.Description: Nice place to see the history of addis Ababa and how it became what it is today. You only pay 10 birr to explore the place and enjoy history. title: Lion of Judah Monument
address: 2Q82+JXP Lion of Judah Monument, Woreda 05, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: Dr. Melaku Taye Amogne
user_reviews.Description:
A Monument Steeped in Ethiopian History and Pride...

The Lion of Judah Monument in Addis Ababa is a profound symbol of Ethiopia's rich history and legacy. As an iconic landmark located in the heart of the city, it is a must-visit for both locals and tourists alike.

As a guy from rural Ethiopia, visiting the Lion of Judah Monument invoked a huge sense of national pride. Its grandeur, which has been masterfully sculpted to embody strength and resilience, is so admirable. The statue stands proudly, exuding a sense of regal dignity that reflects the historical significance of the Lion of Judah in Ethiopian culture and heritage.

The location itself is highly accessible, situated near key landmarks, and easily reachable.
The surrounding area is well-maintained, providing a serene environment for reflection and admiration of the monument. The towering bank headquarters, the distinguished National Theatre, and the charming old Ethiopia Hotel, create a beautiful and historic setting for the monument. This juxtaposition of modern and historical architecture adds to the epic ambiance, highlighting the monument's significance amidst the bustling and dynamic cityscape...

Furthermore, the Lion of Judah Monument serves as an excellent backdrop for photography, with its striking design and the surrounding landscape creating picturesque scenes. It is a perfect spot to capture memorable moments and appreciate the artistic craftsmanship of the statue.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to connect with Ethiopia's storied past and its vibrant present.

user_reviews.Name: fitse wako
user_reviews.Description:
The Lion of Judah Monument in Addis Ababa is one of Ethiopia’s most iconic landmarks, symbolizing the country’s strength, pride, and rich heritage. Located near the National Theatre, the statue holds deep historical and cultural significance, representing the Solomonic dynasty and Ethiopia’s identity as an uncolonized nation.

The monument itself is beautifully crafted, with the lion standing tall on a pedestal, crowned and holding a cross, which adds to its regal and spiritual symbolism. It is not just a work of art but also a powerful reminder of Ethiopia’s resilience and unity.

The surrounding area can be busy, but the monument remains a striking and memorable spot for visitors. It’s a popular stop for history enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone wanting to experience a piece of Ethiopia’s national pride.

Overall, the Lion of Judah Monument is a must-see for anyone visiting Addis Ababa. It’s more than just a statue—it’s a cultural emblem that carries the spirit and story of Ethiopia.

user_reviews.Name: Mikiyas Melkamu
user_reviews.Description: The Lion of Judah Monument is a beautiful and modern representation of the original statue of Lion of Judah. The 10-meter-high black-stone and brick monument was built to commemorate the Silver Jubilee of Emperor Haile Selassie and was a breathtaking experience. The combination of the intricate craftsmanship and majestic stature of the statue makes it a must-see for anyone visiting Ethiopia. Whether you are a history buff or someone simply wanting to experience some of Ethiopia's rich culture, the Lion of Judah Monument will not disappoint.

user_reviews.Name: MiTeku Ayene
user_reviews.Description:
Medhane Alem Church — A Sanctuary of Stillness in the Heart of Addis

Medhane Alem Church is one of those rare places where the noise of a city seems to pause the moment you step onto its grounds. During my time in Addis, I would walk there every morning from my hotel—just a short 10-minute stroll—but the effect it had on my mind and spirit lasted the entire day. There was something profoundly grounding about starting my mornings there, watching the city slowly wake up while the church already felt fully alive.

What struck me first was the atmosphere: calm, almost weightless. Despite the constant movement around Addis, Medhane Alem seemed to carry its own rhythm—slower, deeper, deliberate. As soon as I approached its gates, that sense of serenity washed over me. I don’t know if it was the quiet hum of prayers, the soft breeze passing through the courtyard, or simply the presence of something bigger than myself, but it anchored me every morning. It’s one of the few places where you feel both humbled and lifted at the same time.

Architecturally, the church is an incredible representation of Ethiopian Orthodox tradition, capturing both the ancient and the modern in one monumental structure. The scale is grand without being overwhelming; the domes, arches, and carvings all speak to a lineage of craftsmanship and devotion that has shaped Ethiopia’s Orthodox heritage for centuries. Yet there’s a contemporary sharpness to the design—clean lines, bright stone, and an openness that welcomes both worshippers and wanderers alike. It feels timeless, as if the old and the new are in dialogue rather than competition.

The courtyard becomes its own living story. Elderly worshippers making the slow, intentional walk around the church. Children running with a kind of joyous freedom. Pilgrims lighting candles with quiet faces. Priests moving with purpose in their white robes, carrying an air of dignity shaped by tradition and years of service. Even if you don’t understand the language, you understand the devotion. Being there is witnessing faith in its rawest, most unfiltered form.

Inside, the energy shifts—still peaceful, but thicker, heavier with meaning. The chants, the incense, the intricate religious art, the sound of footsteps against polished floors… it creates an atmosphere that feels alive. You don’t need to be Orthodox—or even religious—to appreciate it. The experience itself is spiritual.

What made Medhane Alem special to me wasn’t just its beauty, though it’s undeniably one of the most stunning churches in Addis. It was the feeling. The grounding. The everyday reminder that stillness can be found in the middle of a bustling capital. For those ten minutes walking back to my hotel, I always felt lighter, as if the world made more sense after stepping inside.

If you’re visiting Addis, go early in the morning. Walk the grounds. Sit for a moment. Let the quiet stretch out around you. Medhane Alem isn’t just a landmark—it’s a place the soul recognizes before the mind does.

user_reviews.Description:
Abune Petros was born in 1892 in a farmer family in the city of Fiche, Ethiopia. At the age of 24 he took the Ethiopian orthodox church oath and became a monk. He grew up and became a well-known teacher around the monasteries in different parts of Ethiopia. His teachings and preaching were very popular and insightful to the people and in 1928 he was nominated to one of four bishops of Ethiopia, with the title and name ABUNE PETROS. He continued to preach the gospel and teach in the churches.

When Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1932, Abune Petros followed with Emperor Haile Selassie and the Ethiopian defense forces to the northern front. He helped the wounded, prayed, consecrated the dead, and preached the Gospel.

ABUNE PETROS executed on 29 July 1936 by the Fascist Italians forces in Ethiopia for publicly condemning colonialism, invasion and massacre. This statue of Abune Petros was raised in Addis Ababa 10 years after his death, as a reminder to future generations of :
•	His strong stand for the truth
•	His unbending courage to stand up against every form of violence against humanity
•	His integrity and commitment not to give in for short-term gain or threat.

1. Symbol of the Ethiopian Monarchy:

The Lion of Judah is a symbol of the Ethiopian monarchy, especially associated with the Solomonic dynasty, which claimed descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.

Emperors of Ethiopia, including Haile Selassie I, used the Lion of Judah as a royal emblem. It represented strength, legitimacy, and divine right to rule.

A statue was erected to Menelik II in 1930 at Menelik square in Addis Ababa. It was designed and made by German Architect Curtin Specingler and unveiled in 1931.
The message on the statue reads: "It is not greatness to hail from a prominent family, greatness (triumph) is to contribute something valuable to the motherland."
The message is clearly written to portray the victory of blacks over white opressors--it shows that the color of skin does not make one race superior and another inferior.

Aba Dagnew was Menelik's horse's name. And it stands on its two legs and face to the north--to signify the direction of the battle field.

The place Menelik II Square, formerly Adawa square, was dedicated to erect the statue owing to its location as downtown of the city during the time, Addis Ababa City Administration Culture and Tourism Bureau Intangible Heritages Senior Expert Memhir Mekibib Gebremariam indicates.
Generally, Menelik II statue and Adwa Bridge, around Megenagna, are among the known memorials of the victory of Adwa in Addis Ababa.
Memhir Mekibib underlines the fact that Addis ought to see more memorials to inherit the sprites to posterity and demonstrate the history to visitors.
I share a little you should visit and see our history.

user_reviews.Name: ኢትዮጵያዊ
user_reviews.Description: The Imperial Palace was begun as a house on a hill built for Empress Taitu who would visit the hot mineral springs at Felweha, a short distance away. The area was named Addis Ababa by the Empress, and a town grew rapidly around the house of the Empress. In 1886, the capital of the Empire was moved to this site from Mt. Entoto, and Taitu's husband, Emperor Menelik II rebuilt the house as his primary Palace. Over the years the Palace was added to and expanded, to include a multitude of buildings of various sizes and functions in a large wooded compound. The Imperial Palace served as the official Palace even after Emperor Haile Silassie I moved his primary residence out to the Guenete Leul Palace in 1932, and it remained the official seat of the Monarchy until the revolution of 1974. The Marxist military dictatorship (known as the Derg) that overthrew the Imperial Government in September 1974 continued to use the Palace as it's official seat of government. The Derg renamed the Palace as the "Grand Palace" but it also used the term Menelik Palace regularly. The extensive wine cellars of the Palace were used to imprison prominent figures of the Imperial government, including male members of the Solomonic Dynasty. It remained the seat of power of the Peoples Republic of Ethiopia when it was proclaimed in 1987 by the Derg, and the current government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia also uses it as it's official seat of power. Emperor Haile Selassie was kept under detention in one of the buildings in the palace compound following his deposal in 1974. He was killed here, and buried secretly on the grounds, a latrine built over the site of his grave. His remains were disintered following the fall of the Derg and he has been reburied. There are three important churches on the grounds of the Palace. The most prominent is the magnificent Ta'eka Negest (Resting Place of Kings) Ba'eta Le Mariam Monastery, with a large Imperial crown atop it's dome, which serves as the mausoleum of Emperor Menelik II, his wife Empress Taitu, and Empress Zewditu, his daughter and eventual successor. The other churches are the Se'el Bet Kidane Meheret Church (Our Lady Covenant of Mercy) and the Debre Mengist St. Gabriel Church. Former President, Lt. Col. Mengistu Haile Mariam converted the house of the Dean of the Ba'eta Le Mariam Monastery, into a large residence for himself, and this building continues to serve as the residence of the Prime Minister of until 2013. This Palace remains the seat of government in Ethiopia, the Menelik Palace has renovated and most part of it has converted to museum and park and open to the public in 2019.

user_reviews.Description:
Where else in the world can you see Lucy, our oldest ancestor? 💕🇪🇹 Only in Ethiopia!

I can not recommend this gem of a museum enough. I'm a lover of natural history museums, and this has the most comprehensive collection of human evolution fossils I've ever seen. It was sheer joy.

Plus, Ethiopian history as well. ❗ Foreigners may be surprised at the depth of Ethiopian history. When Romans were trading, Ethiopians were there with them. Really great artifacts.

💲 Entrance is very inexpensive, we paid 160 birr for two adults and a kid. However, I recommend against the guide. Ours just read the signs aloud and wanted a substantial tip (honestly, I've never had someone tell me the tip I offered wasn't enough, he was only happy with 5 times the entrance fee)

A must-see in Addis!

user_reviews.Description:
The National Museum of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa offers a fascinating look into the country’s rich history and culture. Highlights include the famous Lucy fossil, ancient artifacts, royal treasures, and traditional art. The museum is well organized, and the staff and guides are knowledgeable and friendly.
Overall, it’s an educational and highly recommended place to visit in Addis Ababa.

user_reviews.Name: Scott Forler
user_reviews.Description:
Should be one of the first things to do when you arrive in Ethiopia/Addis Ababa. All informational displays are in English. Upstairs it gives a great overview of the history of Ethiopia going back to 1,000 years BCE covering Ethiopian Antiquity, Christian Kingdoms, Ethiopian Sultantes, and Megalithic Societies. Not a huge display but supported with artifacts and photos of actual sites. Also maps of locations of churches and fossils across Ethiopia. Plenty to see in a day.
Downstairs is the famous Lucy skeleton, both reconstructed and the partial skeleton pieces found. Plenty of information about the origins of our species and some interesting fossils of native animals.

user_reviews.Name: Abraham Yohannes
user_reviews.Description: I really enjoyed my visit to the National Museum of Ethiopia. It was incredible to see  Lucy and other ancient human fossils up close such a powerful reminder of Ethiopia’s place in human history. The museum also has a great collection of royal artifacts, traditional clothing, art, and cultural items that give a strong sense of the country’s heritage. It’s a meaningful and worthwhile experience overall.

We met him when we were trying to figure out which bus to take from the market back to our hotel. The bus driver and conductor didn’t speak English, and with so many passengers rushing in, we were about to give up on taking the bus. Then, by chance, he appeared and helped us. Thanks to him, we made it back to our hotel safely.

Once we experienced it, we realized that the buses in this country are actually quite comfortable, and after that, we had no trouble using them.

We wanted to explore Addis Ababa with his tour, but we already had our schedule planned, so it wasn’t possible this time. Still, the next time we visit Addis Ababa, we’ll definitely contact him and join his tour.

Young Isaac — see you again!

user_reviews.Description:
Meyazia 27 Victory Square is a traffic circle and historic landmark in the incredible neighborhood of ‘Arat Kilo’. Miazia 27 in Ethiopian Calendar (which is equivalent to May 5th) represents both the day when
Addis Ababa fell to Italy in 1936 and was liberated in 1941. The monument at the center of this Square honors the patriots’ fight against fascist Italian invaders, and the victory gained. The monument consists of an obelisk and a relief figure. The obelisk, topped by a Lion of Judah, stands at the center while the relief figure, of Emperor Haile Selassie holding the national flag, encircled the oblisk.

This intersection is surrounded by various significant places like buildings of Ministry of Education, the Parliament, Office of the
Prime Minister, the Palace, Holy Trinity Cathedral, Science College of Addis Ababa University, Menelik II High School and Berhan Ena Selam Printing Press

user_reviews.Name: brhane hailu
user_reviews.Description:
Trinity Cathedral’s Stunning Renewal

The newly renewed Trinity Cathedral is nothing short of breathtaking. Blending historic reverence with modern elegance, the restoration has elevated this iconic landmark into a space that feels both timeless and refreshed.

The interior now glows with renewed light—every stained-glass window seems more vibrant, the vaulted ceilings more majestic, and the acoustics have been subtly enhanced to create an atmosphere that’s both serene and powerful. Whether you’re attending a service, a concert, or simply exploring, the space now invites deeper reflection and awe.

Architecturally, the renovations have respected the cathedral’s original Gothic beauty while carefully incorporating contemporary touches that make it feel more accessible and welcoming. The lighting, seating, and layout all reflect thoughtful attention to comfort and inclusivity, without compromising the spiritual grandeur.

The Trinity Cathedral has long been a cornerstone of the community, but this renewal feels like a bold new chapter—one that honors its sacred past while embracing the future with open arms. Simply put, it’s amazing.

user_reviews.Name: Amanu R
user_reviews.Description:
La Gare is a historic train station located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It was built in 1929 during the Italian occupation of Ethiopia and served as a major transportation hub for the country's railway system. The station's unique architecture, featuring a mix of Italian and Ethiopian design elements, has made it an important landmark in the city.
However, over the years, the station has fallen into disuse and disrepair. The decline of Ethiopia's railway system and the rise of alternative modes of transportation have led to a decrease in passenger traffic at La Gare. The station's once-grand building now stands empty and neglected.
Moreover, adaptive reuse would preserve and revive La Gare's historical and architectural significance while giving it a new lease on life. The station would become a symbol of Addis Ababa's past and present, a reminder of the city's rich cultural heritage and a hub of activity and community.

user_reviews.Name: Mikiyas Melkamu
user_reviews.Description:
The Adwa Victory Center is a project that has been in the works for a few years now, and while it is not yet complete, it is already shaping up to be an incredible destination for anyone interested in learning more about Ethiopia's history.

One of the standout features of the Adwa Victory Center is its focus on the historic Battle of Adwa. This battle was a pivotal moment in Ethiopia's history, and the center is dedicated to educating visitors about the events leading up to the battle, the battle itself, and its aftermath. The center is home to a wealth of artifacts, exhibits, and multimedia installations that bring this moment in history to life in a truly immersive way.

While the Adwa Victory Center is not yet complete, it is clear that a lot of thought and care has gone into its design and construction. The building itself is modern and sleek, with plenty of open spaces and natural light. The center is also fully accessible, with ramps and elevators making it easy for visitors of all abilities to explore the exhibits.

Of course, it is worth noting that the Adwa Victory Center is still a project that is in progress. While there is already plenty to see and do at the center, there are still areas that are under construction or not yet open to the public. However, this should not deter anyone from visiting the center and experiencing all that it has to offer.

if you are interested in learning more about Ethiopia's history, I highly recommend checking out the Adwa Victory Center. While it is still a project that is in progress, it is already shaping up to be an incredible destination that is well worth a visit.

user_reviews.Name: Hussain
user_reviews.Description:
يعد The Skyscraper Tower واحدًا من أبرز المعالم الحديثة التي تجسد جمال العمارة وجرأة التصميم في آنٍ واحد. عند الوصول إلى البرج، يلفت الانتباه أولًا شكله المهيب وارتفاعه الشاهق الذي يمنح الزائر إحساسًا بالفخامة والعظمة. تصميمه الخارجي يتميز بمزيج أنيق من الزجاج والحديد، ما يعكس الضوء بشكل مذهل ويعطي المبنى حضورًا بصريًا قويًا سواء في النهار أو عند إضاءته ليلًا.
من الداخل، البرج لا يقل إبهارًا؛ فالمساحات الواسعة والتشطيبات الفاخرة تعكس مستوى راقٍ من الجودة. يوجد فيه مجموعة متنوعة من المرافق، من مطاعم راقية تقدم أطباقًا عالمية بإطلالة بانورامية على المدينة، إلى مقاهٍ هادئة مثالية للاسترخاء أو الاجتماعات الودية. كما يضم مناطق مخصصة للتسوق الفاخر مع علامات تجارية عالمية، مما يجعله مقصدًا متكاملًا للزوار.
أكثر ما يميز The Skyscraper Tower هو منصة المراقبة في الأدوار العليا، حيث يمكن للزائر الاستمتاع بمشهد ساحر يطل على المدينة من ارتفاع شاهق. المنظر يعطي شعورًا بالتحرر والانبهار، خصوصًا عند غروب الشمس أو في ساعات الليل عندما تتلألأ الأضواء.
من ناحية الخدمات، التنظيم داخل البرج مميز، والمصاعد سريعة وآمنة، والموظفون ودودون ويحرصون على تقديم المساعدة للزوار. الأجواء العامة تجمع بين الحداثة والراحة، مما يجعله مكانًا مثاليًا لقضاء الوقت سواء للسياحة أو للأعمال.
باختصار، The Skyscraper Tower ليس مجرد برج شاهق، بل تجربة متكاملة تمزج بين العمارة العصرية والرفاهية والأنشطة المتنوعة، ويستحق أن يكون وجهة أساسية لكل من يبحث عن المتعة والإبهار في قلب المدينة.

user_reviews.Name: Mohammedkabir Dawud Mohammed
user_reviews.Description:
Grand Anwar Mosque is located in Merkato, in Arada district of Addis Ababa. It was built by the Italian government around 1922. The mosque is the largest and one of the oldest mosques (masjid) in Addis Ababa. The mosque has unique architecture with white and green colors.

After the Italians left unfinished, Muslims collected money to resume the construction. When the construction completed, 16,000 ETB were not paid to the contractor, which led to closure for couple of days by court order. The mosque then reopened as an individual covered payment.

During fasting periods, thousands of people gather in the mosque compound and man can carry incense to smell inside the mosque. A portable podium placed to the middle of green pillars supporting the white outer walls and domes that form spectacular façade of the mosque.

user_reviews.Name: Omo Culture Ethiopian Tours
user_reviews.Description:
Overview

Name: Shola Market (also called Megenagna Shola Gebeya)

Location: Shola area, Yeka Sub-City, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Type: Open-air market

What You Can Find

Shola Market offers a wide variety of goods, including:

Clothing & Shoes: Both traditional Ethiopian attire and modern styles

Textiles & Fabrics: Locally made cotton (shemma) and imported fabrics

Food Items: Spices, grains, fruits, vegetables, meat, and dairy products

Handicrafts & Souvenirs: Traditional jewelry, baskets, and household goods

Household Items: Furniture, kitchen utensils, and electronics in some areas

Atmosphere

It’s a bustling local market, less touristy than Merkato but still full of color and energy. You’ll hear lively bargaining, see vibrant displays, and experience the authentic daily life of Addis Ababa residents.

Accessibility

Easily reachable by taxi or minibus from most parts of the city.

Located close to Megenagna, a major transport hub.

Parking is available, but often crowded.

Tips for Visitors

Best to visit in the morning for fresh produce.

Bargaining is expected—prices are negotiable.

Keep an eye on your belongings, as it can get crowded.

Great spot for experiencing local life and culture.

user_reviews.Name: Alvin Ma
user_reviews.Description:
Mike is a professional tour guide who customized a 4-hour tour based on my tight layover schedule. He joked about Ethiopians' view of time and way of expressing time but is used to western tourists' idea of time based on his relatives' experiences in America. He has strong English skills so communication about many topics was not a problem - we discussed everything from IELTS exams to marathon running, cost of living to Orthodox Christmas fasting schedules. He explained kitfo and khat as he drove through crowded market streets, but trusted me to drive an easy short distance up Mount Entoto. We saw the devotion of Orthodox Christian worshippers at Mount Entoto and Muslims near a mosque along the central merkato district of Addis Ababa. He pointed out that many young middle-class professionals in the city like to use mobile payment systems but older generations outside the city still use cash (similar to other countries). He saved me a trip at a currency exchange (which would have cost me more in transaction fees) by helping me buy coffee grounds at a fair price.

Despite the best quality beans being restricted to the exports market, he still led me to a quality traditional shop with a ceremonial way of serving coffee. He led me to a small Chinatown (which I had known nothing about) and talked about Chinese EV company Build Your Dreams' investment as Ethiopia shifts to a greener economy. There are some blue minibus taxis and stray dogs sleeping under cars on cracked roads, but there are also tree-lined boulevards. Addis Ababa is an amazing city to explore, and I strongly recommend exploring it with Mike of Habesha Wonder Tours.

user_reviews.Name: C. T.
user_reviews.Description: We couldn’t have been happier with Joe as our tour guide for our first time in Addis Ababa. Joe had excellent English communication and insight on how to deliver a tour with the just the right amount of “must sees” and side excursions to see the real city and learn from a local perspective. We never would have been able to cover what we did without Joe. We came away with a good understanding of the city’s various neighborhoods and Ethiopia’s development in a changing region.  We enjoyed seeing the less touristy side of the city, with adventures into the bustling market, a slip into an ethereal prayer service at a local church where we were the only foreigners, and tastes of local coffee and pastry. We would be remiss not to mention what a lovely person Jo is — extremely warm and excited to show us “his country”, he became a friend after our time together and we hope to engage him again the next time we come!

title: The Alchemist Dine & Wine Restaurant
address: African Avenue, Japan Street, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: Samuel Little
user_reviews.Description: What an amazing place to eat! From the moment we walked in, we were warmly greeted by the owner and chef, which immediately set the tone for an incredible dining experience. The cheese appetizer was out of this world—honestly one of the most delicious things I’ve ever had—and it only got better from there. The salad and soup were so flavorful I actually had to pause between bites just to savor them. The spaghetti was fresh, perfectly cooked, and full of unique, memorable flavor. The chef even came to our table multiple times to check on us, making the experience feel so personal and welcoming. The atmosphere and vibe were spot-on, making the whole evening unforgettable. I’ll definitely be coming back again!

user_reviews.Name: Yohannes Berehanu
user_reviews.Description:
Unbelievably good! Food was amazing! The starter bread mix along with their butter selection was AMAZING! Super great service too!

Their flavors are just superb and very reasonably priced for the amount and quality! This is beyond a restaurant. You should be proud for what you have done for our city!

user_reviews.Name: Veronika Kunz
user_reviews.Description: My husband and I had a 7 course dinner at the restaurant. The food is amazing, the portions are big and the service is incredible! Highly recommend this place for a nice night out!

user_reviews.Name: Lubka Mieresova
user_reviews.Description: Great dining experience, a delicious tasting menu and very nice cocktails. The staff was very kind and the place is very tastefully decorated. Looking forward to our next visit!

user_reviews.Name: Yeworkwoha Ephrem
user_reviews.Description:
Three longtime friends recently dined at The Alchemist Dine & Wine, and our experience was exceptional from start to finish. Chef Mekibib Zewdie warmly greeted us upon arrival and ensured we were comfortably seated. Although we initially ordered three dishes to share, the thoughtful additional tastings prepared by the Chef were a delightful and memorable surprise.

The food was outstanding—beautifully prepared and full of flavor. The ambiance was refined and welcoming, and our server was both knowledgeable and genuinely attentive, making sure every detail was perfect.

We will certainly return, and we highly recommend The Alchemist Dine & Wine to anyone seeking an elevated dining experience.Yeworkwoha Ephrem, Ghenet Brooklyn

user_reviews.Name: Sirak Berile
user_reviews.Description: I chose this restaurant for my birthday and reserved a table to have dinner with my wife. I have to say I was VERY disappointed with how dinner went. To start off, when they brought the bread basket, they didn't even give us a full bread basket like the other tables had; we only got the round bread balls, we didn't get any of the sliced bread. The next thing that irritated me when the appetizers arrived was the kids running around chasing each other and screaming; hence why I gave atmosphere a 2/5. If you're a "fine dining" restaurant, the last thing I want is to deal with random kids running around and ruining my experience with their screaming. You should uphold a certain standard if you call yourself a fine dining restaurant. In regards to the food, there's the good and the bad. The good is that the food tasted nice, my wife really enjoyed the different butters that came with the bread and the mocktails were very good. The bad is that the truffle butter and the truffle sauce that came with both our mains had absolutely no truffle in them. I cook with truffle myself and I couldn't smell or taste any truffle whatsoever in the butter or the sauces so it's very disappointing; either put more truffle oil or be honest with customers on whether or not the dishes ACTUALLY have truffle in them. All in all, it was a very disappointing dinner and I don't think I'll be returning unless a lot of things change.

user_reviews.Name: hermela girma
user_reviews.Description: Dining at The Alchemist was an absolute delight! The food was bursting with flavor, beautifully presented, and perfectly balanced. I hade the Chicken Cordon Blu. Every bite was amazing. The service was attentive and warm, and the atmosphere made the whole evening feel special. Highly recommended! I will definitely visit again.

user_reviews.Name: Zina Abebe
user_reviews.Description:
The salads were my favorite it is definitely a must try if you are planning to go there, and loved the white fish as well. The rest was mid (nothing fancy) and some of the foods were a bit salty and some were hard to cut. The other thing I didn't like was their sales approach.
P.S - The detox water was a great bonus

title: Golden Plate Restaurant | Bole | ጎልደን ፕሌት ሬስቶራንት | ቦሌ
address: Abssinia Building, Cameroon St, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

owner.name: Golden Plate Restaurant | Bole | ጎልደን ፕሌት ሬስቶራንት | ቦሌ (Owner)

user_reviews.Name: Adam Jano
user_reviews.Description:
The place is on the second floor, right on the corner of the street (it took me a moment to find it too).
Great spot for both lunch and dinner! The atmosphere is relaxing and the service is excellent. The waitress who served me, “Fre”, was attentive
, friendly, and very helpful.

I ordered the Alfredo and a steak. The Alfredo was excellent, rich and flavorful. The steak was tasty, but a bit too tough for my liking, so I’d probably skip it next time.

Overall, it’s a lovely place to come with family, for a date, or even solo. I’ll definitely be back.

user_reviews.Name: Michel Carus
user_reviews.Description:
The moment I entered the restaurant, the power went out completely, plunging it into darkness.
But nobody seemed to mind!
I was invited in and shown to my table while the waiters placed battery-powered lights on the tables. The chefs continued working by the light of their cell phones over an open fire.
Not a single guest left. On the contrary, new guests kept arriving.
At the end: the beer was cold, the soup was hot, and the bayaynetu was delicious. What an experience!
I'd especially like to commend Fre's service: she was like a shining star in the dark night sky.
One star deducted for the lack of gas for the emergency generator.

user_reviews.Name: Tequam Gebremariam
user_reviews.Description:
Visited Golden Plate last Saturday to celebrate my best friend's birthday. The restaurant was lively and full, which added to the festive vibe. The setup is stylish and welcoming — a great spot for special occasions with friends or family.

Due to the crowd, we had to wait quite a while for our food. While that’s understandable, the delay likely caused the mashed potato, lasagna, and grilled chicken to arrive cold. The mashed potato also lacked flavor. Thankfully, the Chef Henock steak made up for it — juicy, well-seasoned, and clearly the highlight of the meal.

The staff were courteous, and the overall ambience is pleasant. With a bit more attention to food temperature and timing, this place could easily become a top choice.

I’d rate the experience 4 out of 10, mostly for the steak and the birthday atmosphere. I’ve added photos and videos to help others get a better sense of the place.

user_reviews.Name: Thomas “Neverjuststay” 汤
user_reviews.Description:
Indeed, the ambiance, staff service, and kitchen management at ADDIS are absolutely superb.

However, the food is the most important factor in any restaurant.

Our family dined here on Christmas Eve, and unfortunately, as a Western restaurant, there were no Christmas decorations or a Christmas menu. Well, perhaps it's because Christmas here is in January.

The ambiance is suitable for business events and is worth recommending.

The waiters were clearly experienced and trained.

1. Off the three soups on the menu, only the vegetable soup was available. A minus.

2. Off the five desserts, only tiramisu was available, and it took 30 minutes to arrive. It's possible it was a frozen product purchased from outside and needed time to thaw.Or perhaps few people order desserts here, so the owner is under financial pressure and doesn't prepare desserts for the meal.

3. Regarding the cutlery, while they tried hard to follow the standard bistro setting, the main course cutlery was just there, but where were my appetizer cutlery? The steak knife I specifically requested was even less effective at cutting beef than the main course knife. The serving plates were bread plates, not main course plates, and they were all chipped and broken. I simply cannot understand the management's thinking in such a high-end restaurant.

4. Now for the main point: the food. The chef's signature steak, which appeared to be prepared by a live chef, was actually just going through the motions. Moreover, it used rump and topside steak that were practically inedible (we ended up packing it up and giving it to  dogs on the street).

This was definitely a major drawback. Professional chefs have various techniques and skills to handle the taste and texture of steak, yet this restaurant's signature dish was treated so carelessly.

I won't review all the other dishes since I've already written about them.

I hope the manager and owner value the restaurant's beautiful and thoughtfully designed layout, the excellent service staff, and the good kitchen facilities. These are all secondary; delicious food is the most important and fundamental element for a restaurant's long-term success.

I've written so much because I hope you continue to improve and that you'll pique my interest again someday.

First, please change the menu—make it more refined, focus on the taste, and reduce pressure.

user_reviews.Name: mekdes Tadesse
user_reviews.Description: Meron geremew was absolutely amazing — very attentive, friendly, and professional. She made sure everything was perfect and always had a smile. Her service really made our meal special. Highly recommend this place, especially with such excellent staff!

user_reviews.Name: Ethiopia Asress
user_reviews.Description:
Review for Golden Plate – Bole

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Golden Plate in Bole, and I can confidently say it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. This fine dining restaurant truly lives up to its name, offering both elegance and warmth in every aspect.

I ordered the steak, and it was cooked to perfection—flavorful, tender, and beautifully presented. The quality of the food alone makes this place worth a visit.

What truly elevated the evening, however, was the outstanding service. Our waiter, Barnabas Kassa, was incredibly professional, attentive, and welcoming. He made sure everything was perfect throughout the night, and I’d give him a 10 out of 10 without hesitation.

From the ambiance to the service to the delicious food, everything about Golden Plate was spot on. I would 100% recommend this place to anyone looking for a top-tier dining experience in Bole.

user_reviews.Name: Simret Beauty
user_reviews.Description:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Absolutely Outstanding Experience!
We went to Golden Plate Restaurant to celebrate my daughter’s birthday, and we left absolutely speechless! The food was beyond delicious every dish was perfectly prepared, fresh, and full of flavor. The environment was warm, elegant, and welcoming, making it the perfect place for a special celebration. The customer service was exceptional from start to finish. Our server, Beza, was an amazing individual attentive, kind, and genuinely caring. She went above and beyond to make our experience unforgettable. Thank you, Golden Plate, for making my daughter’s birthday so special. We can’t wait to come back again!

user_reviews.Name: Hodzic Saud
user_reviews.Description: The restaurant has a refined interior and a pleasant atmosphere, and the staff are friendly and professional. However, when ordering the house specialty advertised as “steak,” expectations are understandably high. Unfortunately, what I received was not a proper steak but rather a fillet that seemed so tough it felt like chewing gum — an unpleasant surprise for such a well-presented establishment. The side dish also lacked refinement. I’m giving two stars purely for the tasty soup and the courteous service.

title: Cravings Restaurant & Bar
address: XQMW+7VC Cravings Restaurant & Bar, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: Gee-man
user_reviews.Description: Quick, efficient service makes this spot ideal for grabbing a meal before your flight or relaxing during a short layover. While I found their breakfast a bit underwhelming, I’m looking forward to trying other menu options on my next visit.

user_reviews.Name: Kamal Singh
user_reviews.Description:
Too oily food. Soaked in oil.
Takes a lot of time for the food to get prepared.
Drinks are the saving grace.

Just look at the vegetable sandwich. So much oil in the patty. That's not healthy for you.

Prices are too damn high for the food. $22 for an oily sandwich.

Avoid and get something else.

user_reviews.Name: Dom Trejaut
user_reviews.Description: First of all, the spicy berry margarita was the best margarita in Africa thus far! Great spice level for those who like the heat!!!! Excellent range of Ethiopian beers as recommended by our new friend and bartender Teddy! Legend!

user_reviews.Name: Emad Sayed
user_reviews.Description:
The staff is professional and the food is very delicious
The photo is for my regular corner where I used to sit every tim

user_reviews.Name: stanley addo
user_reviews.Description: This place exceeded all expectations! The chef's tasting menu was a culinary masterpiece, each dish a work of art. The staff made us feel so welcome. Will definitely be back!"

user_reviews.Name: Pascal Bondo
user_reviews.Description: Loved our visit! The portions were generous, prices were reasonable, and the food was delicious. A fantastic neighborhood spot with genuinely friendly staff. We'll be back!"

user_reviews.Name: Amihay Shraga
user_reviews.Description: Had a short layover in Addis Ababa and stopped here for a break. It’s not fully Western-style, but definitely the closest you’ll get at this airport. Great beer, fast and friendly service.

user_reviews.Name: maisie kwan
user_reviews.Description:
I had a generally good experience at Cravings, especially if you're looking for a comfortable spot to relax during a flight transfer. The seating area is spacious with plenty of comfy chairs and useful plugs, which made it a great place to settle in and get some work done instead of the lounge.

However, I did encounter an unpleasant situation with one of the staff members. The restaurant was mostly empty at 8 PM, yet I was asked to move from a four-seater sofa to a two-seater to make room for other passengers. This seemed unnecessary, especially when there were barely any other guests around, as shown in the photos. By 8:55 PM, there were only 7 occupied tables, and they even moved another person from a two-seater to the bar, which felt a bit odd.

As for the food, the Ethiopian dishes were delicious, and I recommend them if you're in the mood to try local flavors. However, the pasta portion was quite small for the price.

Overall, Cravings has a great atmosphere for travelers, but I hope the staff can consider a more flexible approach to seating when the restaurant isn't crowded.

$28US for a pasta

title: Yod Abyssinia Traditional Restaurant
address: XQRV+F92 Yod Abyssinia Traditional Restaurant, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: Zerith
user_reviews.Description:
Definitely the best cultural restaurant around. I’ve been to others but Yod Abyssinia wins the cup 🙌🏻
The enthusiasm, joy and friendly staff are excellent.
The food is also really great depending on when whether you like spicy or not and whether you’re a fan on injera or not (it was an acquired taste for me). Being here definitely gave me an authentic Ethiopian experience. It was absolutely worth it.

user_reviews.Name: Kartik Shah
user_reviews.Description:
Wow just incredible. We went for the special vegetarian traditional food and every single item on the plate was amazing. It is a touristy place but well worth it if you're in Addis.

The dancing and entertainment was excellent too.

user_reviews.Name: AMIR BAJWA
user_reviews.Description: Quite an amazing place to enjoy traditional Ethiopian food with cultural and dance show at night. The atmosphere is very friendly and vibrant. The cultural show was very quite fascinating, while food was also good, though one can find better tibs at other places. But, overall, a very nice place to enjoy food, drinks and local songs and dances.

user_reviews.Name: Peter Karanja
user_reviews.Description: Very nice place and a lot of intricate designs embedded in the building. Faiir prices if you factor in the live, professional entertainment. Definitely one to visit for Ethiopian food and culture and not far from the airport.

user_reviews.Name: Urban Ucanjsek
user_reviews.Description:
An amazing experience!
The food was exceptionally good with an outstanding variety of dishes – every bite was top-notch. The waitstaff were friendly and attentive, the place was clean, and the restrooms were well maintained. Small details like bringing a bowl for handwashing to the table really showed care for the guests.

The atmosphere was elevated by beautiful live music and phenomenal dancing – the performers made a real effort to involve the audience, which made it even more engaging. There's also a souvenir shop on-site, which is a lovely touch to end the evening. While it’s a bit on the pricier side, the whole experience is absolutely worth it. Highly recommended!

user_reviews.Name: Hussain Almoamen
user_reviews.Description:
It’s nice but not the best!
I have been to a better one in town, nicer atmosphere, better food and cheaper.
Here is more touristy and pricy.
I don’t really recommend it if you are looking for a good natural experience.

user_reviews.Name: Hanna S
user_reviews.Description: Amazing music and dance shows in the evening, starting approximately 7 - 7:30pm. Table bookings are recommended for evening time. Food was also good

user_reviews.Name: See Addis Ababa Ethiopia
user_reviews.Description:
A cozy and stylish café in the heart of Addis Ababa! ☕🌿
Great coffee, warm ambiance, and friendly service make it a perfect spot to relax, work, or meet friends. Highly recommended! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Marcus Addis Restaurant & Sky Bar
address: Head Office Tower 47th Floor, Ras Desta Damtew St, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

complete_address.street: Head Office Tower 47th Floor, Ras Desta Damtew St

user_reviews.Name: Siye Keberabe
user_reviews.Description:
Marcus Addis presents a truly breathtaking concept. Perched high in a stunning Addis Ababa high-rise, the venue offers amazing panoramic views. The physical space is beautifully divided into intimate settings, a stylish bar, a lounge, and a dinner area all of which are outstanding and worthy of a five-star designation.

I will give full credit where it's due: the ambiance and location are world-class.

However, the experience falls short of its immense potential. For a setting of this caliber, the expectation is a seamless, seven-star, ultra-luxurious, and formally impeccable establishment. Currently, there are significant gaps.

The most notable issue lies in the staff's professionalism, discipline, and general coordination. The service lacks the flawless, anticipatory quality required, from the moment one enters to the moment one leaves.

Furthermore, the food was mediocre. I understand the chef is working hard to pioneer a fusion of Ethiopian cuisine with European influences—an ambitious and commendable experiment. Yet, in its current execution, it does not meet the mark for a restaurant that aims for the pinnacle of fine dining.

In summary, Marcus Advis has all the foundational elements of a legendary dining destination: the view, the location, and the beautiful settings. However, to transition from a place of great potential to an undisputed leader, there is substantial work needed in service execution and culinary refinement. It feels very much like a "work in progress."

user_reviews.Name: Sašo Nožič Serini
user_reviews.Description: Marcus is marvellous place in Addis, you can come just for coffe, drink or two *Bedele Special  (my recommendation) and view, have a Tomahawk (Japanese Beef) a la Chef Marcus's (the place got his name after there one chef) for brunch, lunch or dinner and finish with nice gin and whisky or limoncello. Signature cocktail 🍸 👌 list is nice touch with original Ethiopian Habesha flavour. You will definitely not regret the visit.

user_reviews.Name: A S
user_reviews.Description: Swedish celebrity chef Marcus Sameulson's sky restaurant atop a high rise. Definitely an experience you want to enjoy while in Addis Ababa. The cuisine is African fusion with varying international interpretations. I had the scallops which were forgettable, and I was with a large group so there were too many other dishes to get a vibe. The cocktails were perfection. If you're looking for that celebrity chef restaurant experience, this is the place. There's a DJ spinning and the atmosphere is wonderful. You need reservations and you should dress to impress.

user_reviews.Name: Mic Jr
user_reviews.Description: Stunning view and amazing atmosphere make this fine dining spot memorable. The service is excellent and welcoming. However, the menu is very limited with few options to choose from. While the food tastes good, the lack of variety and value falls short of expectations.

user_reviews.Name: Jamie NS
user_reviews.Description: Excellent food and service and good value lunch menu.  I really enjoyed my visit here, very friendly and well trained staff.  The Malbec wine and steak were excellent.  All on top of the tallest building in East Africa!

user_reviews.Name: Bisrat Abraha
user_reviews.Description:
From the time the reception confirmed my reservation twice at around 11am as I did move my reservation to another date once, I was impressed at their consistency of what time to confirm reservations.

The place was as lovely and even more than I expected and better than all the videos I saw prior to our arrival.

Chef Marcus is talented of course, but better than his amazing talent lies a view and an elevator ride that is worth a visit to this place.

The price is very affordable and my date and I were surprised as we stared at our bill and already planned another visit very soon.

I like to add that you should work on the Wi-Fi service. You shouldn't have a password for it. Phones or other devices should automatically sign into it. I don't think clients will climb a 47 story building just to use Wi-Fi.

user_reviews.Name: Tortura Tarantulo
user_reviews.Description: Yesterday, I spontaneously decided to visit Addis Ababa's tallest building. I found a very pleasant atmosphere in the sky bar and restaurant there. I got a table without a reservation and was able to enjoy a delicious dinner. I had delicious, high-quality food and excellent service. Rachel served me very attentively. I had an excellent dinner in a pleasant atmosphere with a magnificent view of Addis Ababa at night from the 47th floor. As I left the building, I was warmly bid farewell by a young lady, also named Rachel—what a coincidence.

user_reviews.Name: Swiss Note
user_reviews.Description:
I recently had the pleasure of having dinner at Marcus Addis Restaurant And Sky Bar and it was exceptional. This dining experience perfectly represents Ethiopia’s modernisation. It offered a unique consolidation of traditional Ethiopian dishes with western influenced cuisines. Every dish was presented with care. It was a wonderful experience from start to finish.

The restaurant was located on the 47th floor and the view was absolutely spectacular.

The ambience was stunning, magnificent decor, and they brilliantly integrated comfort and elegance.

A special mention goes to staff members, who truly made our evening memorable and we felt truly valued as guests. Post-dinner the staff offered to give us a private tour of the entire restaurant which occupies an entire floor which topped-off our lovely experience. Overall the service was fantastic.

I understand why Marcus Addis Restaurant And Sky Bar has gained traction in the city. It truly exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a terrific dining experience in Addis Ababa.

Side note: We took couple videos which is on our page and linked to Google Maps.

title: Henom Restaurant
address: 2Q79+GHH Henom Restaurant, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: Mahlet Kassa
user_reviews.Description: At the heart of Kazanchis, a fine dining place with good food. Had a pleasant experience in this beautiful place. I loved the painting and the ambience of the restaurant. It has different vibes sitting inside the reaturant, outside and at the bar area, all inclusive. The service was great. The only thing I didn't like was their macchiato. The food was tasty, and presentation was everything. They also do catering. It's definitely a great option for business lunches and a friendly gathering, too.❤️❤️

user_reviews.Name: Sean Martu
user_reviews.Description: The food is pretty tasty, I also really liked the complimentary soup and bread. I'll definitely be coming back.

user_reviews.Name: Dayal
user_reviews.Description: The complimentary starter soup was tasty. We ordered Fish Curry, Chickna Tips, and Ginger Tea. The total came to 1,514 Birr, including 15% tax (1,316 Birr net). While the food was good, the prices are slightly higher compared to nearby restaurants. The staff were polite, but their English skills were limited. We had to rely on body language to communicate.

user_reviews.Name: Naomi Janse van Vuuren
user_reviews.Description: We had an exceptional experience, and will definitely be back soon!! Menu represented traditional Ethiopian food and international choices in a balanced way.  Our food was delicious, and very seductively presented. Arsema was very knowledgeable about dishes and ingredients. Her suggestion about the Nile perch (Tis Abay)  was an absolute winner. Her knowledge and passion was a lovely addition to the ambience of the restaurant.

user_reviews.Name: C M
user_reviews.Description: Best place for me so far. The service is amazing, the food is also really good not substandard. They are also very understanding. I paid twice by mistake and I was able to come the following day and it was sorted. I recommend this to everyone who enjoys good food and service.

user_reviews.Name: Michiko Kaneko
user_reviews.Description: We had a wonderful dinner at Henom tonight. We have been in Addis Ababa for six days and this is definitely the best restaurant we have been. The French fries were crisp, the steak was tender, and the veggies were exquisitely char-grilled. They also have traditional Ethiopian food. The service was excellent, thanks to our attentive waitress Arsema.

user_reviews.Name: Adrianna Glegoła
user_reviews.Description:
Great experience at Hendon restaurant. The burger and salad were delicious, and the creamy soup was especially amazing. :)

Excellent service from Kalid! He is amazing, very kind, helpful. :) It was a pleasure to meet him.

user_reviews.Name: laura bolton
user_reviews.Description: Loved the free starter.   Had cinnamon mojito which was fab. The the nice fish which was ok. Great atmosphere

title: ADD Restaurant | Ethiopian Skylight Hotel | ስካይላይት ሆቴል አድ ሬስቶራንት
address: XQQQ+6W7 ADD Restaurant | Ethiopian Skylight Hotel | ስካይላይት ሆቴል አድ ሬስቶራንት, Airport Rd, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

owner.name: ADD Restaurant | Ethiopian Skylight Hotel | ስካይላይት ሆቴል አድ ሬስቶራንት (Owner)

user_reviews.Name: Marl Molina
user_reviews.Description:
An Absolute Masterpiece: The Grilled Beef at Skylight Hotel Restaurant
Stepping into Skylight Hotel Restaurant immediately sets the stage for a great dining experience. The ambiance is warm and welcoming, matched only by the attentive and friendly service. While the menu offers a compelling array of dishes, today, during lunch, my focus was solely on one item: the famous grilled beef.
And oh, what a delicious reality that meal turned out to be.
Each bite melted away, leaving that satisfying, rich, buttery flavor that only comes from expert preparation and quality sourcing.
It’s clear that this dish is prepared with passion and precision, achieving a sublime texture and flavor that elevates simple grilling to an art form.
My highest compliments, and the reason I’m writing this review, must go to the visionary behind this incredible meal:
Chef AMAN. Thank you for taking such a humble cut of meat and turning it into an unforgettable culinary experience. Also, a huge thank you to our waiter, Gadisa, for providing genuinely attentive and friendly service. Skylight Hotel Restaurant is a must-visit, and you absolutely must order the grilled beef. I’m already planning my next trip back!

user_reviews.Name: Deborah Perinchief
user_reviews.Description:
Though the star ratings speaks volumes, I would like to also personalize, this rating, by expressing our gratitude and sincere appreciation for our waitress, Debora’s professional and caring service.  Lunch was delicious and the ambience soothing after what I can only describe a not so great start to our last day in Addis Ababa.

Thanks again, Debora
From Deb and Phil

user_reviews.Name: A Sajib
user_reviews.Description: Worst food I've tried in Addis. None of the main courses had any flavor or seasonings. The desserts were hard and felt like they had been a few days old. I've never wasted food or returned food before this. It was inedible. Waste of money and time.

user_reviews.Name: Gedion Feyissa
user_reviews.Description: We had a wonderful time at The Terrace restaurant on the 2nd floor. Our waitress Elsa was able to recommend great options for vegans. The whole atmosphere was fantastic.

user_reviews.Name: anuj jagtap
user_reviews.Description: I visited this restaurant during my layover at ADD. I availed the dinner buffet at this restaurant. I loved the Injera and Chicken curry. The jasmine rice was also good. Plenty of desserts were also available and were tasty. They had a couple of vegetarian options as well like chickpea stew and salads. Mr. Zewdu helped me understand the local cuisine and was quite courteous. Will definitely recommend this restaurant for transiting travellers.

user_reviews.Name: Tim Jones
user_reviews.Description: I stayed at Skylight with the included hotel stay with my business class flight. This was the first meal via the included vouchers and it surpassed expectations. My waiter Zewdu was so friendly and helpful!

user_reviews.Name: Fasil Tsegaye
user_reviews.Description: Kalkidan was our waitress; she is highly trained and pays close attention to her tables. We got A level treatment

user_reviews.Name: Δημητριος Παπαιωαννου
user_reviews.Description:
Great food, calm atmosphere. This was my 4th visit, always fresh, good cooking food with plenty of choices.
The personnel working there are helpful but a little more appreciation for  mr. Abayneh for today's help.

Ethiopian airlines are making huge steps beyond to established as one of the biggest companies not only for the fleet size and the destinations they fly to but also in its overall service to passengers.

address: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: B-Shadow
user_reviews.Description:
Pretty nice place with best service,
The interior is great for a date or group vibes,
The food is not bad, their starter salad and sauce is a bomb💣
They got delicious frappuccinos and shakes too

user_reviews.Name: orient travel
user_reviews.Description:
We really liked the food and the hospitality is top plus timing was great.
Name:- Zenaw thank you 🙏

user_reviews.Name: Tibeb Kemis
user_reviews.Description:
Went to try their dubai chocolate cake however was really disappointed. The chocolate sponge layer was burnt and the pistachio is not real, it tasted like white chocolate with green food colouring.

We told the waitress that it was the bottom cake layer was burnt and she just walked off.
Rather than it being a dubai chocolate cake it seemed like a dubai cake from dubai tera 😂😂😂

Don't have High hopes for this dessert st this place unless you want to eat burnt cake.

user_reviews.Name: Mic Jr
user_reviews.Description: Nice interior and chill vibe, seemed like a nice spot. But the lugaimat was just okay not as tasty as the ones i know overall my take is: Overhyped and overpriced. Dont start me on the iced mocha it’s not good at all. Service is slow. Only plus: they’re very generous with pistachio and toppings other than that i donno. 🤷🏽‍♂️

user_reviews.Name: Senit Abreha
user_reviews.Description:
HORRIBLE SERVICE!!!!!

We came here after we saw the paid reviews on tiktok and to say we were disappointed is an understatement. We waited at least 25 minutes without ordering because the waiter kept walking away when we called him. We had to bother the sweet lady by the computers and she went and called him for us twice. After he came, our server, said there are a lot of orders and we won't get what we want. Before he even asked what we wanted. We eventually brought us the wrong thing and when we told him he told us it's not his problem. Horrible experience. 0/10

UPDATE: we ordered the loquma for takeaway and they flat out refused.
Never coming back here again

user_reviews.Name: Henok Ketema
user_reviews.Description: We enjoyed the vegetable sandwich and the chicken nuggets, both paired with a tasty salad and hummus starter. Zinaw provided us exceptional service with a warm smile and professionalism. We are excited to visit the restaurant for a third time before we depart. Highly recommended!!

user_reviews.Name: Adam Mengistu
user_reviews.Description:
Disappointed by misleading pricing and poor service

I visited this restaurant after seeing some great reviews, and while the food was good, the experience was ruined when the bill arrived.

We ordered 3 Mocha drinks, clearly priced at 350 birr on the menu. I even pointed to the item on the menu while ordering to avoid confusion. But when the bill came, we were shocked to see we were charged 700 birr per drink,double the listed price.

It turns out the restaurant uses two different menus with identical drink names (like Mocha and Mojito), but with very different prices. This kind of setup is confusing at best, and at worst, feels dishonest.

It left a sour taste after what could have been a great meal. I hope the management fixes this pricing inconsistency before more customers feel misled.

user_reviews.Name: Hiya Tibebu
user_reviews.Description: So, I had lunch today and it was very disappointing, the food test was good but the portion is very bad. Not even satisfying for one woman. And the service was OK until the waiter forced me to rate him start after taking my phone befor I was even done . And the environment looks good but very unprofessional people. One of the stuff started doing his prayer infront of me while I was eating.... anyhow I don't recommend it.

title: Fafresh Cultural Kitchen - Dembel | ፋፍሬሽ ባህላዊ ሬስቶራንት - ደምበል
address: Shoa Dabo | Dembel, Africa Ave, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

owner.name: Fafresh Cultural Kitchen - Dembel | ፋፍሬሽ ባህላዊ ሬስቶራንት - ደምበል (Owner)

user_reviews.Name: Sean Martu
user_reviews.Description: Love this experience, the Ethiopian coffee culture is definitely something to experience. I had no idea that they burned spiritual residents like frankincense and myrrh to cleanse out your spirit and aura before and while you were drinking the coffee. I'm not even a coffee drinker, and I drink it straight and I enjoyed it I didn't even add any sugar. Customer service is great, and the food was pretty tasty.

user_reviews.Name: Scott Forler
user_reviews.Description:
Being gluten sensitive is not too hard here in Addis Ababa. Much of the food is gluten free. Don’t know about celiac levels of sensitivity and cross contamination.  But Hilary, a member of the family run restaurant, knew a lot and was able to give the rundown on all their dishes. She spoke perfect English and was a very attentive host. I ate here two days in a row to try some more of their delicious food. If you are visiting Addis, this is a great value and comfortable place to go.
I’ve had
-Shiro (chickpea stew)
-Doro Wat (chicken in spiced berbere sauce, eaten with gluten-free injera or rice)
-Fasting Kitfo
-Fasting Gomen Kitfo

user_reviews.Name: Ameha selassie Tibebe
user_reviews.Description: Though I've been referred by a friend some time ago, I first bumped into Fafresh few months back, just for a casual lunch. To begin with, I was impressed by their unique combo varieties on their menu with very reasonable prices, offering  diff. dishes perfect either for single consumption or larger portion for groups.(incl. veggies, meat, cottage cheese, and freshly made Injera and "kocho", a popular local bread from the Ghurage region and most of Southern Ethiopia made from false banana)  Such packages are not common in many traditional "Kitfo" restaurants. As I went on a busy lunch hour, my order took a li'l while but the quality of the food was definitely worth the wait. Within few more visits,  the true dedication, consistency and genuine hospitality of the owners, (two sisters, Hilary & Summer) which has become quite a rare combination of virtues in similar businesses of today's Addis won my heart and made me feel at home at this cozy eatery. Today, I'm not only a regular patron but rather feel like part of the family of Fafresh Restaurant. Kudos to the owners and all who played a role.

user_reviews.Name: Sonia Carrera
user_reviews.Description: I ordered the mixed fasting dish. It was the tastiest food i had in one week in Addis. I loved the texture of the soy pieces, the sauce was delicious and just the right level of spiciness. The food arrived quickly and the service was attentive. Highly recommended.

user_reviews.Name: Jewe Debebe
user_reviews.Description:
I had the pleasure of dining on Kashet at Fafresh Cultural Restaurant, a place that beautifully captures the essence of Ethiopian culture and cuisine through both flavor and atmosphere.

Fafresh isn’t just about dining—it’s about experiencing Ethiopian culture through food, hospitality, and atmosphere. Great atmosphere, great service, and great food all in one place!

user_reviews.Name: A/haq Haku
user_reviews.Description: I would give them 6 stars if it was possible. They have delicious traditional food with a very good service. It feels like home. I highly recommend fafresh to everyone.

user_reviews.Name: Daniel Tamrat
user_reviews.Description: I had the most amazing experience! The food was amazing!!! I recommend the Fafresh Keshet! We went for four and were very full!

user_reviews.Name: Samuel Berhie
user_reviews.Description: I ordered from Fafresh via an ordering app. They made me wait 2.5 hours only to serve the most disappointing "Fafresh Kesht," one of their house specials. The Kai Wot tasted sweet (which it shouldn't), and the butter used on everything wasn't fresh. All in all, it really wasn't a pleasant experience.

title: The Exclusive Restaurant
address: XQVP+Q3C The Exclusive Restaurant, XQVP+Q3X 123, Africa Ave, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: Meazi
user_reviews.Description:
Thank you for making my friend's birthday unforgettable! This restaurant in Addis Ababa is truly professional, with delicious food and outstanding customer service. The staff are incredibly nice and attentive.
Thank you!

user_reviews.Name: Surafel Boss
user_reviews.Description:
Exclusiv Fine & Dining offers an exceptional dining experience from the moment you walk in. The atmosphere is elegant and inviting, with a warm ambiance that makes every guest feel special. The service is outstanding — attentive, professional, and always delivered with a smile.

The food is truly the highlight. Every dish is prepared with care, beautifully presented, and full of rich, balanced flavor. From starters to dessert, you can tell that the chefs put passion into every detail. Whether you're coming for a romantic dinner, a family celebration, or an exclusive event, this restaurant consistently delivers a top-tier experience.

If you're looking for a place that combines luxury, comfort, and unforgettable taste, Exclusiv Fine & Dining is the perfect choice. Highly recommended.

user_reviews.Name: Biruk Gossaye
user_reviews.Description:
Great for your fine dining experiences.
Call to reserve your seats. We were lucky enough to get a table walking in. The appetizers were more awe inspiring than the main dish. Over all a good experience with a lovely staff.

user_reviews.Name: Josh Smalley
user_reviews.Description: An excellent place. Good vibes. Good flavors. Professional staff. A must visit in Addis.

user_reviews.Name: Estifanos Alebel
user_reviews.Description:
The service was outstanding. The staff were friendly, attentive, and really made the whole experience smooth. I especially want to mention Hana, who stood out with her professionalism and kindness. She checked on us at the right times, made great recommendations, and genuinely made the night feel special.

The food? Amazing. Everything was fresh, well-seasoned, and beautifully served. From the starters to the main dishes, you can tell the kitchen puts real effort into quality and presentation.

user_reviews.Name: Wendy Oui
user_reviews.Description:
Feels like dining at a high-end restaurant in Europe.
The ambiance is great, and they serve pasta and pizza as well.

The appetizers and drinks were all excellent.
For the main course, we went with the restaurant’s recommendation and ordered the ribs and tenderloin…
but the ribs were disappointingly ordinary. 😞

I should’ve gone for the tenderloin with pasta or pizza instead.
That said, the atmosphere is truly amazing!

— Oh, and they’re closed on Wednesdays. 😆

user_reviews.Name: Yohannes Tefera
user_reviews.Description: We went on a birthday dinner and the food was outstanding starting from the entree, the steak and the chicken cordon bleu, to the cocktail and desserts as well. When we come to our server girma he was very caring person. He helped us choose foods and drinks that were great to our likings. The manager was a very cooprative and a nice guy who was checking on us every once in a while and make the birthday a day that we will never forget. I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to the staff members especially our server girma and the house manager for making this special day unforgettable. I would recommend this place if you want to have a very chill vibe and good meal or if you have a special day to celebrate this is the right place to be at

user_reviews.Name: Jordan Granger
user_reviews.Description: One of the best steak dinner experiences I have ever had in the WORLD. The food is not only the very best, but the facility, the staff, the culture and environment is unmatched. Come here and you will be treated like family and royalty with the highest of careful, warm service of the most exquisite dining experience of your life.

user_reviews.Name: VINOD KUMAR
user_reviews.Description: One the best restaurants  in town which can cater to all kinds of guests and food . The ambience is  good and staff is also very friendly. The menu is rich and food is also very tasty. . The Vegetarian cuisine is also excellent . The quality and quantity serves a good value for money .

user_reviews.Name: Jode Wardell
user_reviews.Description: If you eat anywhere in Addis, make it The Chill Spot. Utterly wonderful from start to finish. The curry goat was hands-down the best I’ve ever had—perfectly tender, deep, aromatic spice, just stunning. Service was genuinely warm and attentive, and they took gluten-free/celiac needs seriously, making my wife feel right at home with safe, tasty options. This is, without question, the best food I’ve had in Addis by a long shot. And the mutton? Quite honestly the best I’ve had globally. You must try this place—you’ll come back. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

user_reviews.Name: Shot O' Clock
user_reviews.Description: Great spot for late-night Indian food! The staff is super welcoming and the food always hits the spot. Definitely one of my go-to places.

user_reviews.Name: veran ace
user_reviews.Description: Food is great especially if you love Indian food and the atmosphere is cool and chill and its a great place to hangout with family and loved ones.

user_reviews.Name: yourz truly
user_reviews.Description: Such an amazing atmosphere and great vibes,  the name truly says it as it is as it is always a relaxing place to hang out. Customer service is consistently fantastic 💕

user_reviews.Description: The place is nice very good spot to chill the food is decent with good customer service overall I give it 4 out of 5

user_reviews.Name: asif pn

user_reviews.Description: This restaurant was a life saver for me being an Indian. It is clean and serves good portion of tasty Indian and Ethiopian cuisines compared to other food joints in Ethiopia.

The music it self was cool and chilling they rotated performers which kept thing interesting. Was treated well as a tourist. Highly recommend the music tends to start at 7 30 pm

user_reviews.Name: Mazin Abbas
user_reviews.Description:
2000 Habesha Cultural Restaurant delivers the full Ethiopian experience – delicious, authentic food paired with excellent live cultural music and dances that are simply amazing. If you’re visiting Addis for tourism, this place is a must.

The restaurant is clean, well-organized, and has a welcoming atmosphere. Location is convenient, prices are excellent, and the overall value is unbeatable. A perfect spot to enjoy Ethiopia’s flavors, sounds, and traditions all in one place.

user_reviews.Name: Juliana Siapai
user_reviews.Description: I tried the Doro Wot but unfortunately it didn’t meet my expectations. I also found the prices to be on the higher side compared to other traditional restaurants. On the positive side, the atmosphere is pleasant and does reflect a traditional vibe. Personally, I don’t think I will be visiting again.

user_reviews.Name: Hrvoje Petrovic
user_reviews.Description:
They say this is most the authentic Ethiopian restaurant in whole Addis Ababa. I cannot disagree, but I didnt saw them much. I just know the food, the very same food we ate the day before was spmehow even better then here, and for sure it was cheaper. But, here atmosphere is very alive, you have dancers, singers, so it's more about that then food in my opinion. We ordered a lot of food, we ate everything, you will not exit hungry from here. For 3 of us bill was 5229 birrs (in August 2024 that was 86€ + tip).

Edut: In May 2025 5229 birrs is 35€. Inflation? Yes.

user_reviews.Name: Christina Meetoo
user_reviews.Description:
Nice experience for a non-local, to discover Ethiopian food, music and dance. The show was great with excellent musicians, singers and dancers. The dancers are very impressive.
The restaurant is spacious and you can even join the stage to dance at some point, which is fun. Food was good. As a group, we had lots of meat and vegetable dishes served on a large injera, from which we to ate collectively with our hands. A fun experience if you have an open mind.

user_reviews.Name: Suraj Yengde
user_reviews.Description:
one of the best night-outs i had.
music, ambience, dance, culture, food, and service all receive my 5-star.

the entire crowd comprising of various ethnicities, religions, family, young, old, men, women all enjoyed the food and booze and joined the performers. a great cultural experience.

i rarely square the place with 5 stars. make this your to-go place

user_reviews.Name: Norbert Hessenberger
user_reviews.Description: My colleagues and me had during a business trip delicious dinner with wonderful life music . Employees are very friendly and the service is great!
