No elevator. Book breakfast after checking what's available.

user_reviews.Name: Latiesha Johnson
user_reviews.Description:
I initially only booked 3 nights because of the mixed reviews, but my 3 night stay turned into an 11 night stay because Kerubel and the entire staff was so kind accommodating.  My late night check-in was easy.  The next morning when I went down to get some introductory information for Addis Kerubel showed extreme hospitality and was very personable.  He offered me breakfast even though I had missed breakfast by about 30 minutes.  He also gave me good information on where to get my SIM card and how to stay safe around the city.  I was in one of the larger rooms.  I had a comfortable work desk, two chairs and a small table.  The wardrobe had plenty shelves to unpack and the room also had a refrigerator.  The hot water was consistent and the water pressure in the shower was strong.  I had several meals at the hotel because I was mostly in my room working and the food was consistently really good and very reasonably priced.

Things to note:
1.	If you need airport transfer on arrival make sure you speak to someone and confirm.  I booked last minute so I didn’t have a lot of time to arrange the shuttle pick up.  On the 6th I called and didn’t get an answer so I sent a message thru Expedia about needing shuttle pickup at 12:15am on the 8th.  When I landed and called I was told the shuttle had to be pre-arranged and that they didn’t have anybody to pick me up. I took a taxi because I read in another review that the ride should have been 150-200 Birr.  I was over charged 400 Birr so be sure to confirm taxi rates before you ride.
2.	There is no lift but there was someone available to carry my luggage to my 3rd floor room when I arrived and to bring my luggage down for my departure.
3.	If you are sensitive to noise there is the constant running of machinery at the shop next door from about 9am – 5pm.  I am sensitive to noise but it wasn’t that bad if I had the window closed.
4.	There is no air conditioning or heat, but I didn’t find this to be a problem. During the day the temps were about 75 degrees and the room stayed comfortable.  At night the temps dipped to the 50’s but the bedding was plenty to keep me warm.
5.	The power outages that people speak of in other reviews are city wide so you will experience this no matter what hotel you stay at.  They didn’t last too long.

user_reviews.Name: Pradeep
user_reviews.Description:
During my stay of more than a month, I truly felt like I was living in my second home rather than a hotel. Gashaw, Addis, Salem, and every single person I met here were not just staff members — they became my family away from home. The care, warmth, and attention they showed me went far beyond expectations.

From the very first day to the very last, they made sure I was comfortable, safe, and happy. Every detail was taken care of — whether it was before I left for work or when I returned after a long day, the duty managers always checked on me with genuine kindness. The way they welcomed me this year, remembering me from my last visit, touched me deeply and filled me with joy. That gesture alone showed how much they value and cherish their guests.

The service here is simply top-notch. It wasn’t just about fulfilling my needs, but about anticipating them, ensuring I never felt away from family. The memories created in Room 1010 will stay with me forever.

Leaving a place that feels like another home is never easy, but I leave with a heart full of gratitude. Thank you, my Marriott family, for everything. You have given me more than just comfort — you have given me belonging, warmth, and unforgettable moments.

As a friendly suggestion, I would love to see an upgrade in the Internet/Wi-Fi speed and TV connectivity to support seamless pairing with all mobile brands. Since I use Apple, I felt a bit limited at times. I believe enhancing this would make an already perfect stay even more remarkable for every guest, regardless of the device they use.

user_reviews.Description: The staff was exceptionally courteous, kind, and considerate. From the reception to the housekeeping, the restaurant personnel. I appreciate Addisalem and Abel, who both did everything within their power to make my stay more memorable. Addisalem actually went out of her way to get me a huge pack of Ethiopian coffee to bring back home with me. Will definitely visit again!!

user_reviews.Description:
I stayed at this hotel with my husband and our baby girl, and we had such a wonderful experience. The rooms were very clean and comfortable, but what made it truly special was the staff. Everyone from reception to housekeeping, restaurant, and security was incredibly kind, attentive, and welcoming.
They especially adored our little girl, which made us feel even more at home. We are so grateful for the excellent service and warm hospitality. Highly recommend this hotel for families!

user_reviews.Name: Fery Lissanu
user_reviews.Description:
Firstly, I would like to sincerely thank Samson for his outstanding customer service and professionalism. He treats everyone with respect, which is one of the key reasons we keep coming back.

As for our overall stay at the Marriott Hotel in Addis, the location is excellent, and the safety of the hotel is reassuring. One of the major advantages is that it’s an apartment-style hotel, which is very convenient.

That said, I do feel it’s important to mention some areas that need improvement—especially considering that this is a 4.4-star hotel apartment with relatively high pricing. The level of service we received did not always reflect the price we paid. In particular, the room service was below expectations. As someone who has stayed here multiple times, often with children and for extended periods, I believe there’s a noticeable gap between the cost and the quality of service provided.

I strongly recommend additional training for management, front desk staff, and the room service team to ensure the guest experience aligns with the hotel’s standards and pricing.

Lastly, I would also like to thank the rest of the staff for their efforts and hard work during our stay.

user_reviews.Name: Tsion Terefe
user_reviews.Description:
My husband and I are regular Haile customers. We love the brand, and whenever we travel we stay at Haile—as we’ve done in Hawassa and Arba Minch many times. Haile Grand Hotel in Addis continues to impress us with its beautiful facilities, comfortable rooms, and especially the professionalism of the staff. The customer service in all departments is consistently respectful, friendly and welcoming, which is why we keep coming back.

However, there is one thing that stood out during our recent visit: the service at the outdoor seating area near the waterfall. The staff there seemed a bit dismissive, as if our order wasn’t “enough,” which is very different from the excellent treatment we are used to at other Haile locations. It wasn’t a major issue, but it was noticeable.

One small observation: even though the staff are always polite to customers, we noticed on more than one occasion that some staff members were rude or bickering with each other. It would be great to see more consistency in professionalism behind the scenes as well.

Another factor that made our stay a little difficult was the loud music that carried into our room. Because we were traveling with our 8-month-old, the noise disrupted his sleep at night and made it harder for him to settle.

Overall, Haile Grand Hotel remains one of our favorite places to stay, and we appreciate the high standards the brand is known for. We hope the quality we love in Hawassa and Arba Minch is applied equally across all service areas in Addis.

user_reviews.Description:
Dear Hotel Manager,
Day 1
Everything was satisfactory until it came time to go to bed. Unfortunately, the bed was extremely hard, and I was unable to sleep for even a single minute throughout the entire night. I ended up sitting in a chair, and as of 3:20 a.m., I was still waiting for morning to come.

In all my 54 years, I have never experienced a bed so uncomfortable. I am genuinely disappointed, as this has affected what was otherwise a pleasant stay. I kindly ask that this issue be addressed, as a good night’s rest is a basic expectation for any guest.

Day 2
So I finally get a new room, thinking maybe things will finally go right. But of course not. After a long exhausting day, I just want to relax, turn on the TV, and watch a movie. Guess what? No sound. Are you kidding me? I ask to change rooms again, and they tell me, “Sure, tomorrow.” Fine. I wait. The “5 minutes” they promised turns into six freaking hours before anyone actually fixes it. Absolutely ridiculous.

Day 3
I order breakfast, hoping maybe they can get at least one thing right. Nope. What do I get? A cold omelet, no knife, no fork, no salt, no pepper. I call again, they show up five minutes later with — I’m not even joking — an extra juice and a yogurt, still no salt, no pepper. It’s like they’re not even trying! At this rate, by the time I check out, I’ll have enough material to write an entire book of complaints.

user_reviews.Name: Rob Peelen
user_reviews.Description:
Well, let me tell you about one of the coolest landmarks in Addis Ababa - the Medhane Alem Cathedral. This place isn't just any old church. It's actually the largest Ethiopian Orthodox Church in the entire world! That's right - this baby is huge.

The Medhane Alem Cathedral is located in the heart of Addis Ababa, and it's an absolute must-see for anyone visiting the city. The architecture is stunning - think grand arches, intricate carvings, and tall spires that seem to reach up to the heavens.

But here's the thing - this church isn't just impressive for its sheer size. It's also got some pretty quirky features that make it totally unique. For example, one of the highlights of the church is the giant bell that's housed in one of the towers. The bell is so huge that it's said to weigh as much as an elephant! Can you imagine ringing that thing?

Another fun fact about the Medhane Alem Cathedral is that it's actually a relatively new addition to Addis Ababa. The construction of the church was completed in 2007, and it quickly became a beloved landmark in the city. But even though it's only been around for a few decades, the Medhane Alem Cathedral already has a rich history and culture that's beloved by both locals and visitors alike.

So if you're in Addis Ababa, don't miss the chance to check out the Medhane Alem Cathedral. Whether you're an architecture buff, a fan of religious landmarks, or just someone who loves cool and quirky sites, this place is an absolute gem.

user_reviews.Name: pixel vietnam
user_reviews.Description:
St. Raguel Church (Kidist Raguel Bete Kristiyan) is a significant religious and historical site located in the heart of Merkato, one of Africa's largest open-air markets in Addis Ababa.

It belongs to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, and is dedicated to the Archangel Raguel (Raphael). The church's construction began in 1946, commissioned by Empress Menen and Emperor Haile Selassie after their return from exile, making it a symbol of national liberation and faith.

The church's most notable feature is its immediate proximity to the Anwar Mosque. This unique positioning has made St. Raguel a powerful symbol of peaceful coexistence and religious harmony between Christian and Muslim communities in Ethiopia. It remains an important center for worship, especially during its annual feast day celebrations.

user_reviews.Name: Abrhame Zenebe
user_reviews.Description:
In Addis Ababa Diocese, Merkato Market, Etege Menen vowed to build St. Raguel's church if they were victorious. But their vow was not fulfilled. But before they went into exile, the empress wrote a letter and sent it to the chief of the king, Raguel, through the mail, saying, "Put the letter on the throne so that no one will see it when I came." He stayed there until the Italian invasion passed. In 1934 After finding that Empress Menen had kept the letter, they recited the vows they had taken.

Empress Menen gathered the priests of Enteto Raguel and the local people at Enteto and revealed their intention to demolish the existing building and build another one. But the priests and the people suggested that it would be better if he remembered the name of Menelik. But the empress objected to him saying, "I am not a dreamer." Empress Menen asked the experts of the Ministry of Works about the matter, but they got a response that they should not demolish the existing one. Later they left him and decided to work in Addis Ababa.
The first place chosen was Kolfe. But for some unknown reason it didn't work. Mrs. Shwanesh Degfe, who was the heir of Fitaurari, had a land possession dispute with Arab and Adwa merchants.

The biggest problem for Empress Menen was convincing the priests of Entoto Raguel. Therefore, they entrusted His Holiness Abune Basilios* to carry out this work for them. Abune Basilios, who was born and raised in Entoto, after convincing those in various government jobs, called the Raguel priests of Entoto for a meeting. After many disputes and arguments, the surviving priests said that if Abune Basilios allowed Raguel's ark and relics to come to Addis Ababa, he would give the city and rural land to the priests Being eager for the land and fearing the condemnation, the priests agreed.

0

The work of Mercato Debre Hail Raguel Church started on May 1, 1946. When the work began, Empress Menon, Emperor Haile Selassie and Abune Basilios were present. After consecrating Raguel first, they took the priests and went down to Mercato. Abune Basilios blessed and the king laid the foundation stone. In Girond (later Fitaurari/ Reta Gebre God/Etege Menen Gedrasena/Ato Seyum Akale Wold were assigned to follow the work. The work cost three hundred thousand /300,000/Bir and took two years.

One day in September 1948. On the eve, the ark came out accompanied by the priests and the nobles. The local Oromo people who were confused by the situation protested the situation. The elders and mothers pretended to be weeping. On St. Raguel's Day, the Mass was celebrated in the presence of the king, the queen and Abune Basilios. On the day of the celebration, many of the priests of Ento Raguel regretted the fact that they were not invited to the banquet held at the birthday hall/ today's Addis Ababa University.
From September 1948 From then on, Saint Raguel, the head of Addis Ababa Mercato, started managing both councils. But because the parish was cooling down, it did not satisfy those who were serving in Ento, according to the request of the community of Ento, His Holiness Abune Tekle ordered the return to Ento. Although it was intended to be implemented, it was postponed for three days in May, fearing the riots that might arise.

On that day, Magabe Kahnat Amaya Wolde Jesu, who was the manager of the archbishop at the time, went to the parish under the orders of Abune Gerima. Abune Gerimana and the chief priests were saved by the flower, but the shepherd priests were slaughtered and died. The parish was founded in 1965/66. And in 1977 Also, recently, in 1992, with the money donated by Father Shesha for nothing. It has been renewed.

user_reviews.Name: brhane hailu
user_reviews.Description:
The Bahta Mariam Church is absolutely beautiful! The architecture, peaceful atmosphere, and spiritual presence make it a wonderful place to visit.

Bahta Mariam Church, located in Addis Ababa, is an Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo church with a rich history. It was built in the early 20th century during the reign of Emperor Menelik II and dedicated to Saint Mary. The church’s name, Bahta Mariam, means “Glory of Mary.” It is known for its traditional Ethiopian church design, adorned with beautiful paintings and religious icons. Over the years, it has been a place of worship, community gathering, and cultural heritage for local Christians.

We had a great time visiting the church, it was both inspiring and peaceful. I would highly recommend it to anyone exploring Addis Ababa!

user_reviews.Name: Abrhame Zenebe
user_reviews.Description:
When Emperor Menelik II passed away, his remains were laid to rest in the Besal Bet Kidane Miheret Church, which was his house of prayer. His Majesty the Queen Mother Zewditu proposed that a high monument be erected in his memory as a reminder of his good deeds. In this regard, His Majesty the Emperor Haile Selassie I (then the heir apparent) in consultation with the nobles, magistrates, high officials and dignitaries, authorized the expenditure of hundreds of thousands of dollars from the royal treasury; and it was decided that his memorial be erected on one gasha (400,000 square meters) of land that was the king’s garden and park and was located within the grounds of his palace.
The construction of the church was completed in 1909.  The construction site was cleared, rocks were broken down with a hammer, soil was dug, and the ground was leveled. The work of laying the foundation, which required great care, took months. In 1910 AD, under the leadership of the Archbishop, His Holiness Abune Mathews, a sermon was preached, the Gospel was read, and the blessing ceremony was completed, and the foundation was laid.

In this way, the work of this building, for which the foundation was laid, took ten years. On December 3, 1920 AD, in the era of John, the Holy Spirit of the Holy Spirit (later His Holiness Abune Sawiros), a blessing mass was performed in the church, and the Ark, which came from Gondar, was solemnly entered the church built for the Virgin Mary.  On the same day, the remains of Emperor Menelik II were taken from the Kidane Mihret Church, where they had been resting, and were placed in a tomb prepared for them in the basement. It is noteworthy that December 3/1906 AD was the day Emperor Menelik II passed away. The name of this monastery was decided to be called the Menelik II Memorial Monastery, named after King Ata Lammariam.

user_reviews.Name: Muluken Girma
user_reviews.Description:
Washa Mikael (or Washa Michael) is a unique ancient church near Addis Ababa which is carved out of rock. According to locals, Washa Mikael rock hewn church dates back to the Axumite Kings of Ezana and Sayzana. Priests tell you it was founded in the 4th Century AD.

I visited Washa Mikael rock-hewn church with a couple from Australia on Oct 30, 2022. I find it very interesting. The road to the church is in very good condition (still under construction). There are no road signs on the main road.

If you want to drive to the rock church of Washa Mikael, if you are driving from the British Embassy to Megenagna, take the asphalt uphill road on the left – passing the British Embassy and some compounds, and before reaching Sholla Market Traffic light.
Drive straight uphill until you reach a burial ground on your left. Take the first turn off to left, and drive for about 3 kilo meters.
You will find the church on your left with a corrugated iron fence painted with the Ethiopian colors of Green, Yellow and Red.

There are no official tour guides during my visit. It is advisable to have a tour guide who knows the location and the history. Or make your own preparation in advance.

Washa Mikael rock church is a great substitue to have an idea of the rock hewn churches of Lalibela and such architectural style.
But, it is sad to know the church was destroyed by bombings by Italians during the Italian Occupation.

Have a nice visit!

MKC enjoys a well-deserved reputation for its strong leadership and sense of community. The leaders exemplify humility, compassion, and a genuine dedication to the congregation. The church's sense of community is strong, fostering connections and support among members.

In conclusion, Misrak Meseret Kiristos Church offers an exceptional spiritual experience. From its inviting location to the thought-provoking teachings, and from the dedicated Sunday school teachers to the strong community bonds, the church stands out as a place of growth and connection. Kidane Mihret(Covenant of Mercy)--Monthly feast of Emebetachn(St.Mary)
On every 16th day of the each Month,the Orthodox Tewahedo Church commemorated our Holy Lady Mary,the two-fold Virgin,the God-bearer,for on it He gave her the Covenant of Mercy and She received it from Her Son,our Redeemer Jesus Christ,in respect of him that should celebrate Her commemoration,or should call upon Her name, or giv...e alms to the poor in Her name, even if it were only a cup of cold water.
Our Mother asked Her beloved Son,Jesus Christ(praised be His Holy Name) to save anyone who would pray or do works of charity in her name.And Her Son promptly replied:I will fulfill all your petitions My Mother! I will save anyone who built churches in your name,who clothed the naked,visit the neck,feed the starved,drink the athirst in your name!
This is the Covenant 'Iyesus Kirstos' (Jesus Christ) made with the our Queen!

user_reviews.Name: Henok AD
user_reviews.Description:
A Heartfelt Review for Liza School (1991–2000 E.C.)

I had the privilege of attending Liza School from kindergarten through elementary between 1991 and 2000 E.C., and I can confidently say it was one of the most formative experiences of my life. The school laid a strong educational foundation—not just academically, but in values, discipline, and character.

What made Liza School truly special were the people behind it. Liza and her father, Gira Azmach Belete, were more than just administrators—they were like real parents to all the students. Their kindness, presence, and genuine care for every child made the school feel like a second home. They knew each of us by name, and their doors were always open with smiles and encouragement.

The teachers were just as nurturing and committed, and the environment was one where we felt safe, supported, and inspired to grow. The friendships I made and the lessons I learned have stayed with me to this day.

Now, as a parent myself, I can say with confidence that when my daughter is ready for school, I will proudly send her to Liza School. I know she will receive not just an excellent education, but the warmth and values that shaped my own childhood.

Thank you, Liza School—and thank you, Liza and Gira Azmach Belete—for being such a meaningful part of my life. May God bless you all abundantly.

user_reviews.Name: Matthew J.
user_reviews.Description:
Amharic lessons here were not for me and I cannot recommend this  program. Instructor canceled classes and classes were often interrupted with phone calls. Instructor used free version of Zoom which required logging off and logging back on during class. There were no course materials and instructor became defensive when I asked for materials to preview. Instructor has no background in education and his method is teacher-centered with him speaking, in English, about Amharic for a large percentage of the course. I came to course already knowing how to read and write Fidel and with experience using various resources (Appleyard, Leslau, PCV Amharic Grammar) so it was not a question of my lack of ability or lack of motivation which causes me to not recommend this course, but rather the delivery method.

After 4 classes I realized that the class was not an efficient use of my time and brought this up to the instructor. He became defensive again would not even acknowledge my points about the class, noting that I was the only one who had ever given him this kind of feedback. I tried to discuss his teaching methods with him, so that I could understand more and believe in his approach. However, he was unaware of basic concepts in Adult Education and Second Language Acquisition.  I asked for a refund and the instructor refused. I put my money where my mouth was, even though I paid more than the course fee (for 12 sessions) I was willing to let that money go rather than sit through an hour of him talking about Amharic with no lesson plan. I would suggest asking for a demonstration class before paying money upfront for the 12 courses, perhaps his method is for you, but it was not for me.

I notice positive reviews and perhaps the other reviewers had different learning goals. Also notice that most of the reviews are for the English course and not the Amharic course. Also note the website speaks of “staff” but as far as I can tell it is one person doing everything. I think that if one has the goal of serious learning and ongoing learning, one is better off going elsewhere. I wonder also what the level of the reviewers were before the class and then after the class.

user_reviews.Name: Mahir Mohammed
user_reviews.Description: I’ve prayed at Kera Selam Mosque on numerous occasions, each time marveling at its profound blend of artistry and spirituality. The mosque’s architectural grandeur is unmatched: its exterior showcases intricate geometric patterns and arched doorways rooted in traditional Ethiopian-Islamic design. Inside, the space transforms into a sanctuary of serenity, where meticulously crafted wooden prayer panels and handwoven floor mats mirror the vibrant hues and motifs of the wall paintings. This visual harmony—between the earthy tones of the carpentry and the vivid blues and golds of the murals—creates an atmosphere of unity and reverence. The ergonomic layout of the prayer niches, carved with precision to support worshippers’ posture, exemplifies the mosque’s fusion of beauty and practicality. Beyond its physical splendor, Kera Selam stands as a living archive of Ethiopia’s Islamic heritage, preserving centuries-old craftsmanship while fostering spiritual connection. Its design transcends mere aesthetics, embodying a sacred dialogue between faith, culture, and community identity.

user_reviews.Description:
Well... This center is incredibly amazing with good , clean , classy interior designs .
It currently has a laundry service on ground level (sunshine laundry), an Islamic book store(Aqsa books store) and several boutiques for men and women and just above there is a museum which is constantly developing. On the next floor, there is a research center . The rest of the building until floor#5 are 3 apartments on each floor and just above that on the roof is a newly built studio (BBS ). When you go outside of the studio there are ropes for hanging clothes . (for the people who rent the apartment) . There are 2 basements the lowest basement is for parking cars of the people who live there . Overall it is amazing 🙂 , VERY close to abadir Masjid , on the main Street .

For people who live there the voice of cars passing at night, dogs barking and all that is a bit hard to get used to  . You would think with all of that facilitates you might not get privacy . Surprisingly...the privacy is AMAZING!!!though the place could use a little bit more people who work there .Eg: when there are events ,meetings or trainings... The elevator gets crowded and sometimes misused by kids . So somebody could be in there escorting and helping everyone . There was a time me and my family literally waited for 30 mins .
Sometimes the guards lock the front door for security reasons and then I won't be able to go for a run unless I use the basement (which one day I was almost hit by a car).

Also some sort of guest entry system , to prevent robbery and getting the door of the resident barged open again and again because they ' 'thougt' it was a library (It was seriously annoying). And lots of other things that need management . I suggest trying to communicate with people who live there . So that you can understand and solve problems

This  has been to the most comment I have written Ever😀😀 I wrote it as a constructive feedback . I mean each and everything . 🙏

user_reviews.Name: Manuel Jesús Padilla Domínguez
user_reviews.Description:
The Heart of Ethiopia Has a Name: Yihun and Sisay

We spent 20 days traveling through Ethiopia — a country as fascinating as it is complex. But what truly made this journey unforgettable was experiencing it alongside Yihun and Sisay. They weren’t just our guide and driver; they were the soul of our trip, and choosing to travel with them was the best decision we could have made.

Yihun is the kind of guide every traveler dreams of: deeply professional, always attentive, and with a calm presence that makes you feel safe from the first moment. His knowledge of the country — its history, its culture, its people — is vast, and he shares it with passion and respect. He made sure every single day went smoothly, shielding us from scams and inconveniences, and ensuring we could simply enjoy and learn. But above all, he’s a kind, generous, and honest human being. I brought back many memories from Ethiopia, but his friendship is by far the most precious.

Sisay, our driver, was another gift. In a country where traffic rules seem to be merely suggestions, he was a constant source of safety and peace of mind. He drives skillfully and carefully, always with a big smile on his face. He kept us entertained during long drives, shared the music and rhythms of each region, and was equally curious and open to hearing music from our own country. His joy, warmth, and attentiveness made him much more than a driver — he became a beloved travel companion.

Ethiopia can be a challenging destination, but thanks to them, it felt welcoming, human, and full of light. They showed us their land with pride, dedication, and a level of humanity that’s rare to find. By the end of the trip, saying goodbye brought a lump to our throats and the certainty that we were leaving behind two real friends.

If you’re thinking of traveling to Ethiopia, do it with them. They are exceptional professionals and even better people. Thanks to Yihun and Sisay, we didn’t just discover a country — we discovered its heart.

user_reviews.Name: geni tsiyon
user_reviews.Description:
We were picked up by our guide (Solomon) at our hotel in Semera and off we went to the first Ertale. During the entire trip Solomon showed us that we is an experienced driver and guide. He showed us the best spots in Danakil Depression & made sure to include us in the decision making of where to go or when to leave. The accommodations was open tents  were amazing. The first night was actually very windy. The other one night were basic camp sites but that was half of the fun. To stay and sleep surrounded by mountains and rivers is equally exciting
Make sure you bring warm clothes as well as a flashlight and a powerbank to be prepared. You can charge your phone often but it is nice to be able to do it in your tent as well if needed.

Do not worry about the quality or quantity of the food because there will be an abundance of food each meal. The chef made excellent meals all day long.

The most important thing during this trip would probably the salt lakes, wow! There were so many and Solomon made sure we saw each and every one of them. You could tell he is an experienced guide by the way the communicated with the others via radio and found every hidding place of the animals. It was very exciting all day long!

Overall this was one of the best experience of my life and I would greatly recommend booking your experience of Danakil Depression with Aman Ethiopia Tours. They are truly the best. I could talk for hours about this trip but I will let my pictures do the rest of the “talking”.

user_reviews.Name: Sabina Wojciechowska
user_reviews.Description:
We had a two-week tailor-made trip organized with Aman Ethiopia Tours and the experience was exceptional from start to finish. The team was highly professional, friendly, and attentive to every detail, and we felt very safe and well taken care of throughout the entire journey. The itinerary they crafted allowed us to experience Ethiopia’s incredible diversity—from the timeless rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and the castles of Gondar to the Blue Nile and Awash Waterfalls, and the beautiful shores of Lake Tana. Each place left a lasting impression, and we truly felt that we were in great hands the whole time.
Highly recommended for anyone looking to explore Ethiopia in an authentic, safe, well-organized, and personal way.

user_reviews.Name: Andre Muhammad
user_reviews.Description: I spent 3 days in Addis Ababa before heading to Kenya to visit family, my first time visiting Ethiopia. I wanted to learn of the rich history and culture there. I reached out to Aman Ethiopia tours and wow they did not disappoint. The communication and professionalism was top tier, honest work ethic and integrity impeccable. My tour guide Abe reminded me of one of my College History Professors, extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the history of Ethiopia. I did the city tour on day 1, day 2 was given a personal driver to drive me around (had to check out a spa and do some shopping lol), day 3 was just wow, out in the country side visited the amazing Adadi Maryam Rock Hewn Church, Tiya Stele, and the Melka Kunture Archaeological Sites, all were breathtaking experiences!! Thank you Abe and The Aman tour team for helping create a life time memorable experience, looking forward to coming back soon!

user_reviews.Name: Yalemzewed Girma
user_reviews.Description:
As a current student, I’ve witnessed firsthand the deep-rooted issues within this institution. The administration operates with authoritarian control and widespread corruption. Major decisions that affect students are made without thoughtful analysis or consideration of the consequences. Their leadership is marked by insensitivity, repression, and a blatant disregard for student welfare.
Nepotism is rampant  positions and privileges are often handed out based on personal connections rather than merit, which undermines fairness and excellence. Many staff members display unprofessional attitudes and treat students with hostility or indifference.
Although they claim to be the top institution in Ethiopia, their behavior contradicts that reputation. They reflect a system plagued by corruption, ignorance, and regressive governance. To truly reform this institution, the entire administration must be dismantled and rebuilt with transparency, accountability, and a genuine commitment to education.

user_reviews.Description: Ethiopian Commercial Bank is an old and historical institution that has been around for a long time. While they used to have good service, I found that they have become quite lackluster in recent years. The customer service is not up to the mark, and it can be quite frustrating to deal with the staff. Additionally, the old historical building they used to operate from had holes in the roof that were covered with plastic coverings that looked like something a street vendor would use. However, it's worth noting that Ethiopian Commercial Bank has since moved to a new and bigger building, which is a positive development. While we can not forget the past, it's important to acknowledge that the bank has made efforts to improve its facilities. Overall, while I appreciate the historical significance of Ethiopian Commercial Bank, I think they need to do a lot more to modernize their operations and improve their customer service if they want to remain relevant in today's world.

user_reviews.Name: maranata geday
user_reviews.Description:
MUST READ IF YOU WANT TO SAVE YOUR LOVED ONE!!!!!!!
I am writing to formally express my dissatisfaction and disheartening with the treatment my sister received at Landmark Hospital from the 2nd of May to the 5th of May. My Sister's experience at your facility has left me deeply concerned about the quality of care provided and the professionalism of your staff.

On the 4th of May, I visited my sister in the ICU Department or ward on the 3rd floor as my sister was transferred from the ward to the ICU. Unfortunately, the care my sister received was far below the standard I expected. Specifically, I experienced the following issues:

Firstly, The doctors and the Nurse as well as the supervisor ( a lady who was telling me she had been in nursing practice for more than 14 years?) who were working that night shift had no clue what they were doing with my sister's condition.

Although I politely asked one of the doctors regarding my sister's condition and for an update, he couldn't explain it properly instead he was upset! I believe that as a healthcare professional, it is vital to update family members or the next of ken what's happening or if any progress in the patient's care.

Despite my sister being in severe pain, and discomfort as well as cold to touch they didn't cover her. I asked the nurse if I could bring her blanket but they refused and told me The hospital policy doesn't allow anyone to bring any kind of stuff! which I respect But how can you leave a patient who is hypothermia uncovered?????

Secondly, the saturation prob wasn't working?! I had to use my own and am glad I did cause they couldn't pick up an accurate reading before that. About midnight, my sister started desaturating. they told us they wanted to put her in the breathing machine and intubate her.  I asked the Dr that if she required CPAP or BiPAP, but again the Dr had no clue. He doesn't know what I am talking about despite I explained to him the entire time. Unfortunately, my brother had to sign for consent as I refused to do it so I know it won't make any difference to my sister's condition cause again the doctors don't know what they are doing! Trust me!

They failed intubation! As I am waiting in the corridor with my other two brothers, I can hear my sister's gaggling sound. How can you intubate a patient while awake??????

Soon after, the doctors came out to update us and told me that they failed intubation due to “ fluids coming from her lung”

How can you bring up fluids during intubation????? and not aspiration??? I challenged the Dr who left me and walked away. SAD!

In addition, they waited until the morning at 6:00 am or 12:00 local time to deliver the sad news that my sister passed away 😭
The most painful part was they didn't allow her to rest in dignity as they were trying to resuscitate her despite there being no sign of life.

Additionally, The attending doctors and nurses were dismissive and unprofessional, failing to provide my sister with the right treatment.

These experiences have not only caused me significant distress but have also undermined my confidence in the care provided by Landmark Hospital. I believe that the issues I encountered reflect broader systemic problems that need to be addressed to prevent future occurrences.

I request a thorough investigation into my case and a detailed explanation of why these lapses in care occurred. Additionally, I would appreciate knowing what steps will be taken to ensure that other patients do not experience similar problems. I am also seeking an apology from those responsible and any appropriate compensation for the distress and inconvenience caused.

I hope for a prompt and satisfactory resolution to this matter. I look forward to your response within the next 14 days. Should I not receive a satisfactory response, I will consider escalating my complaint to the relevant health oversight authorities.

Thank you for your attention to this serious matter.

Sincerely,

Maranata

user_reviews.Name: Lulit Gualu
user_reviews.Description:
It has now been two months since I lost my beloved mother, and these have been the most difficult times for me and our family. She spent one month in the ICU at Washington Medical Center before peacefully passing away, and during that time I witnessed the extraordinary care, compassion, and professionalism of the staff.
A very special thank you to Dr. Eshetu. Your professionalism, exceptional commitment, patience, and personal care for my mother stood out in every way. You took the time to listen, to explain, and to reassure me when I felt overwhelmed. The compassion and attention you gave brought tremendous comfort to both my mother and to my family, and I will never forget your kindness.
I’m also deeply grateful to Dr. Jemal, Dr. Surafael, Dr. Tola, and Dr. Feven for their dedication, medical expertise, and for treating my mother with dignity and respect throughout her stay. Their guidance and support gave me strength in such a difficult season.
To the nursing team, my gratitude is beyond words.
Nurse Dawit, my mom passed away while you were giving her such compassionate care. Knowing that her final moments were spent under your kind and attentive watch is something I will always hold in my heart with gratitude.
Nurse Addis, I am forever grateful for your wonderful and tender care for my mother during her last night.

When Meqrez Hospital first started operating, they were known for excellent customer service. But from my recent frequent visits, I’ve noticed that they’ve completely lost their reputation. Today, for example, I saw a doctor in the morning who ordered lab tests, an X-ray, and an ultrasound, and asked us to return at 7:30 pm . However, by the time we arrived, we were told she had already left and would return by 3:00 pm. Now it’s almost 4:30 pm, and she still hasn’t shown up, while I’m waiting with my 80-year-old father. When we asked the nurses, they kept saying, “she is coming,” with no clear response.
This is extremely frustrating and disappointing. On top of that, the hospital recently increased the doctor consultation fee from 800 to 1500, which is a shocking 110% increase. It feels like their focus is more on making money rather than providing quality healthcare. If they want to maintain their name and reputation, they urgently need to revise the way their staff operates.

user_reviews.Name: Unfiltered Service Ratings Ranking
user_reviews.Description:
For some of you giving a one star, please read my comments here. It sounds like you've had a challenging experience at Meqrez Hospital, and I appreciate your perspective on the situation. While my recent visits have highlighted some concerning issues regarding respect and professionalism, I also recognize that one incident shouldn't determine the reputation of the entire establishment or all the doctors within it.

Before writing a review, I encourage everyone to consider the age of this hospital and its status as a newly emerging institution. For instance, during my last visit, I encountered a different doctor who was genuinely attentive and took the time to explain my father's treatment options in detail. This experience reminded me that many healthcare professionals are dedicated to providing excellent care, despite the challenges they may face.

I want to clarify that I don’t work at this hospital, but I am familiar with many healthcare facilities. I believe your comments regarding the hospital may be a bit unfair, especially considering its potential as a promising establishment. It’s essential to evaluate each situation on its own merits rather than rushing to conclusions about the entire institution or its staff.

It's important to remember that circumstances beyond a doctor's control, such as traffic delays or unforeseen emergencies, can happen. Being patient during such times is undoubtedly human and realistic. We should strive to be understanding, knowing that everyone in the healthcare field is working hard to provide the best care possible.

Regarding the recent increase in consultation fees, I understand that inflation and the costs of imported medical supplies are factors that can contribute to such changes. It’s essential to consider these realities when evaluating the pricing. Nonetheless, addressing the overall quality of service is vital for maintaining the hospital's reputation.

If Meqrez Hospital aims to uphold its name, I believe that communication and transparency about expectations and delays could go a long way in improving patient experiences. I hope constructive feedback can lead to positive changes for both patients and staff alike.

user_reviews.Description:
A Formal Complaint Regarding My Hospital Stay – July 3–7, 2025

"The superior man understands what is right. The inferior man understands what will sell." — Confucius

I am writing this letter to express my deep disappointment with the services I received at Silk Road Hospital during my admission from July 3 to July 7, 2025. While your hospital promotes itself as a leading healthcare institution in Ethiopia, my experience revealed a very different and troubling reality—one that puts profit before patient care.

Excessive Pricing Without Matching Quality
I was charged more than what a 5-star hotel in Addis Ababa would cost per night, yet the basic amenities—such as food, water, and room conditions—were severely lacking. I did not come to your facility for leisure or luxury, but for urgent medical treatment. What I received in return felt more like exploitation than care.
Inhumane Treatment of a Diabetic Patient
From the very first night, I was denied access to proper food and water. Despite being a diabetic—a condition clearly noted in my admission records—I was not provided with a meal plan that matched my dietary needs. I was instead handed menus offering items like Kay Wot, Alicha Wot, Dulet, Spaghetti, none of which were appropriate for my condition.
To make matters worse, I was not allowed to bring bottled water from outside. The hospital insisted I purchase their own overpriced bottled water—sourced from the same market, not treated in any special way, yet sold at four times the local price. I became dangerously dehydrated after nearly 20 hours without water, and only after repeated appeals and the intervention of the attending doctor was I finally allowed to drink.
3. Poor Facilities and Risky Environment
The condition of the room and facilities was unacceptable. The bathroom was poorly maintained, and I almost slipped on the wet floor. No safety measures were in place, and no staff offered assistance. Such negligence is not just inconvenient—it is dangerous.
4. A Support System Focused on Profit, Not Patients
While I have no complaints about the medical staff, who were competent and respectful, the hospital’s support system was unprofessional and unprepared. The so-called patient coordinator acted more like a rule enforcer than a caregiver, showing zero compassion or flexibility.
Your hospital seems to operate more as a profit-generating business than a place of healing. In contrast, I recall hospitals in Ethiopia in the 1960s—government-run, few in number, yet known for their exceptional care and human-centered service. Sadly, your institution falls short in comparison, despite charging exorbitant fees.
I am not writing this out of malice, but from a sense of responsibility. I feel obligated to share this experience publicly so others can make informed decisions about where to seek care. I also strongly urge the Ethiopian Ministry of Health to investigate hospitals like yours, which appear more focused on revenue than healing.

Reputation is earned through consistent, compassionate service—not by marketing slogans or inflated ratings. It takes years to build trust, and only moments to lose it.

I am an extremely disappointed patient. You took a substantial amount of my money, which I paid without hesitation, trusting I would receive appropriate care. Unfortunately, that trust was broken.

I hope this letter prompts sincere reflection and immediate corrective actions from your management.

Sincerely,
Bisrat Demis

user_reviews.Description:
I have been a customer of Hallelujah Hospital for the last four years, mainly for child care services. Recently, my wife gave birth, and we are currently still at the hospital.
On the positive side, the hospital is clean, and the doctors are kind, professional, and supportive. We have generally been satisfied with the medical expertise provided by the doctors.
However, there are some serious concerns. The waiting time is extremely long, and the main issue, in my experience, is the nursing staff. Many nurses are not professional in how they communicate with and treat patients. They often act as if they are the sole decision-makers and do not listen to patients or family members. Their attitude can be rude, which adds unnecessary stress—especially in maternity and child care situations.
If you read most of the reviews, you will notice that criticism is mainly directed at the nursing service. I strongly believe hospital management should take this feedback seriously and invest in proper training and supervision for the nursing staff.
We pay for healthcare to receive care and respect, not mistreatment. As a customer, I am not saying do not go to this hospital, but I strongly advise others to consider both the positive and negative aspects before decision.

Gandhi Memorial Hospital (GMH) is one of the oldest public hospitals in Addis Ababa, located on the Ras Desta Damtew Street just next to the headquarter of the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE). The GMH, established in 1959 GC, is a pioneer in maternal & neonatal health services in Ethiopia.

The hospital was named after the world renowned Mahatma Gandhi, an Indian lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer who became the leader of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India.

Recently, the hospital upgraded increasing its hospital bed capacity to 350. GMH is directly operated by the Ministry of Health, providing medical services, particularly focused on reproductive, maternal and neonatal health.

Lancet Behrawi Hospital is, without a doubt, one of the most caring and professional medical institutions I have ever encountered. The doctors, nurses, and staff at this hospital exemplify true dedication and compassion in their work. From the moment we brought my father to Lancet Behrawi Hospital, we were met with an extraordinary level of care and concern.

My father had suffered greatly at the hands of several private hospitals, where he was not only mistreated but also brutally scammed. These experiences were nothing short of a nightmare, casting a shadow over our lives and causing immense distress for our family. We felt hopeless and distraught, unsure of where to turn for genuine help.

However, everything changed when we arrived at Lancet Behrawi Hospital. The staff welcomed us with open arms and hearts, demonstrating a level of intentionality and commitment to helping that we had not encountered elsewhere. They treated my father with the utmost respect and kindness, ensuring he received the best possible care.

Their professionalism is matched only by their empathy. Each member of the hospital, from the administrative staff to the medical professionals, showed an unwavering dedication to my father's well-being. They listened to our concerns, provided comprehensive and compassionate medical care, and guided us through each step of the healing process.

What stands out even more is their fairness in pricing. Unlike other hospitals in Ethiopia, where exorbitant fees are often charged without justification, Lancet Behrawi Hospital offers extremely fair pricing. This transparency and honesty in their financial dealings are rare and deeply appreciated.

Thanks to the incredible team at Lancet Behrawi Hospital, my father is on the path to recovery. The gratitude we feel is beyond words. This hospital has not only restored my father's health but has also restored our faith in the medical profession. They have given us hope and peace of mind in one of the darkest periods of our lives.

Our family is forever indebted to Lancet Behrawi Hospital. We will always remember the kindness and professionalism they have shown us. Thank you so much for everything you have done. Your dedication and care have made an indelible impact on our lives, and for that, we are eternally grateful.

user_reviews.Description:
I walked in to Nordic without an appointment, not realizing they don’t typically accept walk-ins. Still, the staff went out of their way to accommodate and scheduled me in, just an hour later — and, by great luck, with the remarkable Dr. Eman.

Since that first visit, Dr. Eman has become our family’s go-to physician in Addis. It’s rare to find a doctor who is not only highly skilled but also takes the time to truly listen, ask thoughtful questions, and show genuine care for her patients’ well-being. Her follow-ups, attention to detail, and personal investment in our health have made a lasting impact.

To be honest, Dr. Eman is the reason we continue to choose Nordic, even amidst the pricing concerns others have mentioned. Her level of care and professionalism is something you can’t put a price on. My Experience at Nordic Medical Centre
I recently visited Nordic Medical Centre after a friend's recommendation. I needed to see a cardiologist due to an abnormal EKG result from my annual work physical as a firefighter.

Smooth and Efficient Process
- Staff and doctors put me at ease, reducing anxiety.
- Everything was fast and easy from appointment to getting necessary documents for work.
- Consulted with Dr. Hanibal, who sent me for an echocardiogram at Addis Cardiac Centre.
- Dr. Eshetu reviewed results, answered questions, and completed company documents quickly.

Impressed with Nordic Medical Centre
- Cleared for work within a week (usually takes weeks/months).
- Facility is clean, hygienic, with modern equipment.
- Doctors are knowledgeable, humble, easy to talk to.
- Nurses are knowledgeable and patient.
- Receptionists are fast and precise.

Thanks
Special thanks to Dr. Hanibal, Dr. Eshetu, Nurse Mekdelawit, and the reception staff.

I'll be using Nordic as my primary care facility while living/working abroad.

I also would like to add that everything was very affordable, unlike the U.S. where you need insurance for anything medical.

user_reviews.Name: Andrew Morris
user_reviews.Description:
I had need of a RT-PCR covid-19 travel test that needed to be administered with 24 hours of the swab being taken to comply with entry requirements for my destination.  The Suisse Clinic in Addis Ababa, met that requirement and at an affordable price, when compared to Europe.

The booking was simple, complete through an exchange of emails and very friendly.

On the day of my appointment I rolled up promptly, went to reception, paid my dues and went to a tented area to be processed.  It was necessary to bring a paper copy of the photo page of one's passport and a copy of the ticket receipt, which I hand over to the lady at the testing tent. I also completed a form giving my details again, full name as in passport, nationality, passport number, local phone contact etc.

All completed, I went for the swab of the throat and nasal passage. It was a tad more aggressive than ones I had experienced in the UK, but not to bad. Start to finish was 7 minutes.   Worthy of four or five stars no less.  But wait you gave 2 stars.  Well.......

The next morning I got a call.from.the clinic to say I got a negative test and I could collect my certificate that afternoon.  So I trundle up at 1500 or so and ask for my certificate. After a little scurrying around they found it and I checked it over.
They had not of it my surname.on the form, after informing me that they needed all my name's, as per my passport.  Not only that they got my nationality wrong as well.  Considering they had a great copy of my passport with those details on I was a little irritated.  They explained that the lab completes the certificate, so they call them.to explain, but the lab said they could do nothing and that most of the name was correct and should be okay.

I explained that it may be okay for ethiopia, bit some countries checked everything to ensure that things are above board.  Anyway they said to try it or I could retake the test and they would correct it then.  Well that I could not do, So I kept my fingers crossed.

It turns out that embarkation and my destination did a cursory glance looking for the date of the test and result. So it turned out okay.  When I left london's a couple of weeks ago, they checked everything matched up.

The two stars is because an automated system where I enter my details then they pass it on, or verify would, most likely, have ensured that these details were correct.  Photocopies of passports obviously do not help, and a handwritten form is asking for trouble if the space to write names isn't available.

Anyway, I know that the Suisse clinic is a great medical centre for most things, they just felt.short on this.

user_reviews.Name: Yidedya Mehdi
user_reviews.Description:
Devastating Experience - Preventable Loss

I am writing this review with a broken heart to share the tragic and preventable loss of my mother due to what I believe was severe medical negligence at this facility.

What Happened

My mother walked into this hospital  in perfectly fine condition, seeking treatment for a medical emergency. The hospital performed an endoscopy, which should be a routine and safe procedure.

However, the care that followed was nothing short of negligent:

- Despite still being sick, they discharged her and told her she had recovered and could go home on Wednesday.
- Despite coming back in for a medical emergency on Friday, she was told to come back on Monday
- When Monday arrived, the hospital postponed her follow-up care until Tuesday morning
- My mother passed away Monday morning/midnight - before the scheduled Tuesday appointment

The Reality

My mother entered this hospital walking and alive. She trusted this facility with her care during a medical emergency. Instead of receiving the urgent attention she needed, she was sent home and told to wait through the weekend.

She never made it to that Tuesday appointment.

Why I'm Writing This

I'm sharing this painful experience because:

1. Families deserve to know** about the quality of care at this facility
2.  Medical emergencies require urgent care** - not appointments days later
3. No other family should experience this preventable tragedy**
4. The hospital needs to be held accountable for this loss

Warning to Others

If you or your loved one has a medical emergency, please carefully consider whether this facility can provide the urgent, attentive care that emergency situations require. My mother's life depended on proper post-procedure monitoring and timely intervention. She received neither.

In Memory

My mother deserved better. Every patient deserves better. She walked into this hospital alive and left in a way no family should ever have to experience.

When blood pressure is  80/60 it is unsafe to have a routine endoscopy.

Sedation can lower blood pressure even more, which can cause:

For this reason the hospital should stop trying to perform endoscopy . I hope more caution and supervision on the part of the hospital is required to ensure no medical error occurs

user_reviews.Name: Seble Girma
user_reviews.Description:
I am writing what I experienced following the admission of a patient on November 21.

The patient was taken to the emergency room around midnight, and based on the doctors' recommendation, we consented to admission for monitoring. A prior deposit of ETB 30,000 was made, and the patient was admitted to a room by approximately 3:00 AM.

However, from the time of admission until at least 7:30 AM, there was a complete absence of medical staff attending to the patient. We received no updates and had to repeatedly seek out nurses ourselves to deliver lab samples. It was only after our fifth or sixth follow-up that a doctor arrived at 7:45 PM. This doctor then proceeded to question his colleagues at the bedside without speaking to or acknowledging the patient's family, and subsequently left without providing any information.

When we inquired about the medicines being administered, the nurses and the on-call doctor responded with noticeable irritation. The overall experience has been profoundly frustrating. If the purpose of admission was simply for us to wait without active monitoring or communication, we could have done so more comfortably at home.

Furthermore, we were informed that all lab results are normal, yet the patient is being kept hospitalized without a clear medical explanation. This creates a serious misunderstanding and presents the hospital as an organization more concerned with financial gain than patient welfare.

My grandma was admitted to the emergency ward for gastrointestinal problems and later found out about other complications, so she got admitted. After the admission, we waited 7 days for treatment by us, nagging the nurse and doctors, and they asked us to interpret the X-ray, so we had to contract a professional outside the hospital  Also, the head nurse asked us to send her pictures of the saturation level via her Telegram. I hope you understand how unprofessional and unethical this is. The nurses are not fit to handle a critical patient; they tried 5 times to get one canula in, so one of us had to fix it. We tried to contact the manager but couldn't find any responsible person. They gave us a number to report the complaint, which is the reception number, and they wouldn't contact us to the manager. This explains the unethical behavior and lack of discipline in the hospital. Finally, the Available doctor takes orders from the main doctor who was not at the hospital, so they had to call to find out the next step. Imagine the delay when you look for urgent care that you paid for. We had to remind them of their medication and call them to even change positions. No follow-up was communicated to us; we had to ask 100 times. It feels like school rather than a hospital.. so don't Take Anyone You care about and need urgent care to this hospital.

Wound got infected after 3 days, went at 11pm, doctor dressed the wound and told us come back in 24hrs.

Went back 24hrs later, and the doctor on duty refused to believe us, said we should have come in the morning as he believed we'd been instructed, shouted at my poor wife with puss coming from her stomach, that we'd woken him, literally tore my wife open in anger by pulling her skin apart until the stitches tore open, he then soaked a gauze in iodine and reached inside my wife and scraped aggressively several gauze loads of iodine, then sent us away with the wound still gaping.

As a result, for the first week of our son's life, my wife couldn't sit herself up or move unaided, her milk didn't come due to the agony, our baby got anaemic and sick.

We told another doctor and he made excuses. Didn't want to push on case we ended up in an emergency with the appalling, criminal doctor.

Half the staff are ok, mopping up brutal damage of other half who are dangerous and should have their licenses cancelled. Awful. Still have flash backs of his appalling butchery.

user_reviews.Name: Bikila Etana
user_reviews.Description:
They did everything in their power to save my father, but ultimately, no one obviously could alter the inevitable course set by God. Despite his passing, the doctors and nurses provided unwavering support. My father, unable to speak in his final moments, conveyed his appreciation for the nurses through writings and gestures. The entire staff, including guards, kitchen workers, Shukuri, and the medical team, demonstrated incredible professionalism. While I don't know specific names, specially certain nurses stood out in my memory.

Another point worth pointing out is that I provided feedback on ICU services while I was there supporting my father, and I appreciate the professionalism shown by Dr. Moke and the ICU head in addressing those issues, which is not very common in Ethiopia.

For minor improvements, I suggest placing trash bins in the compound, placing hand sanitisers at the entrance, stocking common antibiotics and medicines in the internal pharmacy, and ensuring the reception provides adequate information to new patients and their families. It seems the receptionists are more focused on transactions than providing helpful information.

Thank you all, and keep up the commendable work!
